00290bb7079d83ef.description: ORAC Gallery is developing a focused, curated presentation for its official Booth #2102 at Spectrum Chicago 2026. We are particularly interested in artists with a distinctive and recognisable visual language, a consistent professional practice and a body of work that can function strongly within an international art-fair context. 04952c338d9b63ca.description: The Inaugural Ming Fay Research Fellowship supports the production of original, archives-based scholarship on [Ming Fay](https://www.mingfay.com/) (1943-2025), whose multidisciplinary practice bridged sculpture, drawing, installation, ecology, and transnational cultural histories. Born in Shanghai and raised in Hong Kong, Fay settled in New York in the early 1970s and became part of the downtown art milieu. He co-founded the Epoxy Art Group (1982-92), an Asian American artist collective that fostered alternative exhibition platforms and critical dialogue. While interest in Ming Fay's work has grown through exhibitions at institutions in recent years, scholarship on his practice remains limited. This fellowship supports research conducted within the [Ming Fay Papers](https://findingaids.library.nyu.edu/fales/mss_599/) held at the Special Collections of New York University, related holdings at [Asia Art Archive](https://aaa.org.hk/), and materials housed at the Ming Fay Studio / Estate to support the development of work that contributes to the study of Ming Fay's practice and its broader historical, cultural, and artistic contexts. Proposals may address, but are not limited to: ecology and environmental thought; transnational identity and migration; Asian diasporic histories; material experimentation and sculptural practice; intersections of art, science, and spirituality; nature as mythology and cultural symbolism in art; Downtown New York art networks and artist collectives; and public art and site-specific installations. Grants will be made at one of two levels described below. **Research must be conducted between January 4-December 10, 2027.** **_Fellowship Tracks_** **Senior Research Fellowship** Supports sustained archival research across all New York City-based partner institutions. Fellows are expected to produce a work of original scholarship that advances critical discourse on Ming Fay's practice. Final projects should be developed to a stage suitable for publication, academic dissemination, exhibition development, or inclusion in a larger scholarly project, and may include an article for submission to a peer-reviewed journal (approximately 6,000-10,000 words), book or dissertation chapter, critical essay for publication in a museum, academic, or arts publication, or substantial research toward an exhibition. **Exploratory Research Fellowship** Supports short-term archival research across all New York City-based partner institutions. Fellows are expected to produce a research project demonstrating sustained engagement with the archival materials and contributing new perspectives on Ming Fay's work and related fields of inquiry. Projects are not limited to, but may include a research paper, article, report, dissertation chapter, documentary film, essay, or exhibition proposal. **Deliverables and Reporting** All fellows are expected to produce original research grounded in archival materials and must submit (via email to [apa.institute@nyu.edu](mailto:apa.institute@nyu.edu)) the following deliverables by January 31, 2028: * Final research project appropriate to the fellowship track as outlined above * Brief report (2-3 pages) summarizing research activities, archival engagement, and outcomes
04952c338d9b63ca.restrictions: other: **Senior Research Fellowship Eligibility:** Professors, established independent scholars, curators, postdoctoral researchers, and advanced PhD candidates **Exploratory Research Fellowship Eligibility:** Master's students, early PhD students, emerging scholars, artists, and curators
04952c338d9b63ca.title: Ming Fay Research Fellowship 2027

05757e8d2df17a86.description: Located underneath L'Objet Trouvé in Prague, FOUND OBJECT is a recently opened art space dedicated to experimental, process-based, and cross-disciplinary artistic practices. Following a summer break, the group exhibition **_Works in Progress_** will mark the reopening of the space and act as an introduction to its curatorial direction: open, playful, research-led, and attentive to artistic processes as much as to final outcomes. For this exhibition, we are looking for projects that approach the artwork not as a final, fixed object, but as a creature, system or entity that unfolds over time: through research, interaction, collaboration, repetition, failure, play, or transformation. We welcome works that are literally unfinished, ongoing, or still evolving, as well as finalized projects that reveal the process behind their making. The exhibition can also be an opportunity for artists to present their work in a different way - by sharing sketches, research material, documentation, trials, fragments, or unfinished stages that would be otherwise left unseen. We are especially interested in works that are interactive and/or playful, social, research-based, experimental. All media are welcome, with a particular interest in installation, low-tech interactive experiments, documentary practices and participatory formats. Artists are encouraged, but not required, to continue developing or activating the work during the exhibition.
05757e8d2df17a86.title: WORKS IN PROGRESS

The theme of this year's installment is _The Individual and the Collective_. This year's area of investigation is _The Individual and the Collective_. Successful submissions may include but are not limited to works investigating the dynamic interrelation and compromises between the rights of the individual and the rights of the collective, humankind's nature as a group of individuals or as a collective entity, the formation of civilizations and societies and their associated ethical codes, the role of the individual in shaping collective values, the role of the collective in shaping individual values, etc. From the UN: **_"What Are Human Rights?_** _Human rights are rights inherent to all human beings, regardless of race, sex, nationality, ethnicity, language, religion, or any other status. Human rights include the right to life and liberty, freedom from slavery and torture, freedom of opinion and expression, the right to work and education, and many more. Everyone is entitled to these rights, without discrimination."_ Successful submissions may include but are not limited to works which engage in scholarly research, artistic investigations into archival or literary material, intuitive artistic and/or poetic exploration or expression, designing experimental systems to test an artistic or literary thesis and the subsequent presentation of these outcomes, documentation of one's objective or subjective reality, etc.

0a33376746685d06.description: **$30k USD competition** **"Friction-maxxing is a labour of love"** A prevailing message in our commoditized social sphere is to avoid hard things because they will break you. And yet today we are left more fragile than ever. If only trees could talk. They would tell us as they show us that **flourishing requires friction.** Bending with the headwinds forces trees to develop stress-wood in their core, making them resilient to breakage. Paradoxically trees that are grown in calm, artificial and controlled dome environments frequently collapse under their own weight. As humans, we too are designed to become resilient in the face of life's challenging headwinds; for mysterious reasons, our flourishing requires a character call to deal with friction. In his article ["Friction-maxxing is a labour of love"](https://www.seenandunseen.com/friction-maxxing-labour-love) Samuel Tranter positions the 2026 buzzword _friction-maxxing -_ the intentional embrace of inconvenience in a world of technological ease - into the interpersonal sphere: _'It would be callous to disregard the many hurtful experiences of interpersonal interaction that could lead someone to prefer the company of a chatbot... When the people who actually love us respond to our prompts and attend to our needs, they do not simply give us what we think we want, on demand and without delay. They do not blandly affirm our intentions and our plans... The people who actually love us are unpredictable and inconvenient.'_ It is true that attending to relationships demands a huge amount from us. It was like this before the digital age of LLMs and is more challenging now as strategies of avoidance and dismissal take hold. But what if we step up, '_finding ourselves called to love's demanding work - discovering that we are ourselves the cause of much of the friction'?_ **As artists, how can we bend into today's prevailing headwinds ~ for flourishing ~ where friction-maxxing is a labour of love?**
0a33376746685d06.title: Be Still Media $30k competition - Prompt #28

0d5547616cf02f2f.description: Crafts represent a beautiful combination of cultural heritage, technical knowledge, creativity, and local identity. Across Europe, however, many traditional skills are facing serious challenges due to an ageing workforce, shifting markets, and a lack of educational pathways. Building directly on our ongoing mission to overcome critical data gaps, this new research will join our existing library of seven milestone sectorial studies. Together, this growing body of data helps us deeply understand the sector's vulnerabilities, build collective resilience, and strengthen our advocacy for European crafts. We are looking for an expert consultant or research entity to undertake a comprehensive European study on rare and endangered crafts. The goal is to provide actionable evidence on the current state of vulnerable crafts and propose strategies to safeguard them for future generations. The selected research partner will focus on the following key areas: * Analysis and Mapping: Evaluating the current landscape and mapping endangered crafts alongside existing support structures. * Data Collection: Gathering qualitative and quantitative insights from craftspeople, educators, and policymakers across Europe. * Identifying Best Practices: Highlighting successful initiatives that preserve, transmit, and revitalise craft skills. * Policy Formulation: Creating clear, actionable recommendations for regional, national, and European authorities.
0d5547616cf02f2f.restrictions: other: **Deliverables**: A comprehensive final report, a short policy brief, and a public webinar presentation of the findings.
0d5547616cf02f2f.title: Research Proposals: Rare and Endangered Crafts Across Europe

0fa3503fcb45301d.description: Artists and writers of international, national and Texas origin are invited to apply for two-month, funded studio residencies to produce work in rare scale and focus, with generous support and immersive space, in an historic setting fifty miles south of Dallas, Texas. Residents are hosted at 100 West - a vast, two-story former Odd Fellows lodge, virtually unaltered since its 1890s construction, preserved and minimally furnished with pieces designed and built from the first-floor wood shop. Private artist studios are 2,400 square-feet; writing studio is 600 square-feet; kitchen and dining room are shared. Studio work is prioritized and complemented by introductions to professional networks and world-class institutions in North Texas. This residency takes place in downtown Corsicana - the birthplace of the Texas oil industry and the intersection of this country's cultural and geographic South and West. Oil booms in the 1890s and 1920s produced an exuberant setting, which declined in care and use by the late 20th century before reviving in the last decade. The complex story of rural and small-town America contributes generative context to this residency experience and consequentially enriches contemporary art and literature. **2-Month Terms:** 2 Artists and 1 Writer hosted each term: * WINTER: January 4 - February 23 * SPRING: March 1 - April 27 * FALL: October 11 - December 7 **Expectations of Residents:** * Studio focus and productivity is the first priority; social programming is second. * Self-directed and self-sufficient without need for studio production help. Occasional support is available. * PRESENTATION: second Thursday of residency: 20-minutes, Artists project image / video / slideshow of past work. Writers deliver readings. * OPEN STUDIOS: last Saturday of residency from 12 - 4 PM.
0fa3503fcb45301d.restrictions: other: International, United States, and Texas-based eligibility. Sound-based work is generally not hosted. Performance, composition and sound-based applicants should inquire before applying by contacting residency director to ensure the residency can support their practice successfully. Ceramic, fiberglass and aerosol-based work not accommodated.
0fa3503fcb45301d.title: 2-Month Funded Artist & Writer Residency

14942b736cd51c77.description: South Arts is pleased to announce the FY26 Emerging Traditional Artists Program (ETAP), a component of the **In These Mountains,** **Central Appalachian Folk Arts and Culture** initiative and, new for FY27, expanded capacity building to emerging traditional artists in **Native and Delta Regional Authority** communities. This program recognizes and supports a new generation of traditional artists that have demonstrated a high level of skill in, commitment to, and leadership in their traditional art form. Eligible artists **must** meet one of the three criteria: * Reside in an Appalachian Regional Commission-designated County in Alabama, Georgia, Kentucky, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, or Tennessee. * Reside in a Delta Regional Authority-designed County in Alabama, Kentucky, Louisiana, Mississippi, or Tennessee * Be a member of a state or federally recognized Native American tribe **The following will be funded:** * 12 artists TOTAL in ITM (Appalachia) Region (3 from Kentucky, 3 from North Carolina, 3 from Tennessee, and 3 from expanded ITM area of South Carolina, Alabama, Georgia, and Mississippi) * 6 artists TOTAL in DRA (Delta Regional Authority Counties: Reside in a Delta Regional Authority-designed County in Alabama, Kentucky, Louisiana, Mississippi, or Tennessee) * 6 artists TOTAL from Natives communities (must be a part of federal or state recognized tribe) Awards provide financial support to ETAP participants to ensure the continuation of traditional knowledge and artistic skills within their cultural communities. Traditional art forms may include, but are not limited to: foodways, material culture (handcraft), storytelling, music, etc. Examples may include, but are not limited to: Overshot weaving, Cherokee basketry, Memphis jookin dancing, Mardi Gras Indian suiting, Catawba pottery traditions, quilting, traditional Vietnamese medicine, Guatemalan embroidery traditions, and many more. Selected ETAP artists will receive $5,000 awards (with limited restrictions) to support learning opportunities including training, networking, and promotion. These opportunities should equip traditional artists to expand their own knowledge/practice and to increase the impact of their work within their communities. In addition to cash awards, selected artists will participate in a series of virtual networking and team-building workshops with other ETAP awardees, at no cost to themselves, and will be paired with a member of a previous ETAP cohort for peer mentorship. **What are folk and traditional arts?** The South is home to an abundance of folk and traditional art forms. Folk and traditional arts share the aesthetics, practices, and values of families, geographic communities, occupational groups, ethnic heritage groups, etc. Folk and traditional arts are learned orally, or by observation and imitation, often through a mentor artist instructing an apprentice. They are usually maintained without formal instruction or academic training. Some traditional arts have a deep-rooted history with little change, while others are constantly evolving and adapting to their changing environment. South Arts recognizes that traditional arts in the South encompass a rich diversity of practices, cultural communities, and histories. Applicants must reside in the South to be eligible; however, eligible traditions are not limited to those that originated in the region. Artists may represent traditions rooted in communities with origins outside the South, including traditions that have been sustained, adapted, and blended across generations of Southern life. Program Goals For emerging traditional artists who have demonstrated a commitment to their artform and community and exhibit a high skill level, this award will provide resources for learning opportunities that would otherwise be inaccessible. Learning opportunities can take many forms. Here are a few examples: * Online opportunities for continuing education and collaboration. * Establishing/growing network by traveling within their respective region/tribe or beyond to meet other leaders/potential mentors in your art form. * Taking courses and purchasing software/hardware needed to build an effective online presence. Ultimately, each awardee has the freedom to determine their own learning opportunity-on their own or, if they wish, with assistance from South Arts staff and/or mentors/leaders within their own communities. Funding has limited restrictions, and awardees are not required to submit a final report, produce commissioned work, or engage in any public program. Through the series of professional development convenings and peer mentorship, ETAP is designed to build long-term relationships between traditional artists across the region, beyond state and local boundaries, through: * Building a cohort of emerging traditional artists from Central Appalachia, Delta Regional Authority, and Native communities who are committed to the advancement of folk and traditional arts. * Encouraging and equipping artists to be advocates for their traditional art forms and for the traditional culture of their communities. * Deepening participants' understanding of the importance of public arts support in the United States. Awardees will sign a letter of commitment expressing their intention to participate in ETAP and to attend two virtual workshops and one in-person convening. Over the course of the award period January 1, 2027 - June 30, 2027), recipients will participate in a recorded interview with South Arts staff or other representatives about their art and the learning experience resulting from their ETAP award.
14942b736cd51c77.restrictions: other: To apply for the Emerging Traditional Artist Program, you must: * Be an individual folk or traditional artist. * Be in the early stages of your career/practice. * Be at least 18 years of age by the application deadline of September 30, 2025. * Be a United States citizen, lawfully admitted to the U.S. for permanent residence, or have permission from the Department of Homeland Security to work permanently in the U.S. * Meet the following: * Have been a resident of a county designated by the Appalachian Regional Commission in Alabama, Georgia, Kentucky, Mississippi, North Carolina, South C
14942b736cd51c77.title: Emerging Traditional Artists Program

This year's theme, **PRISMA**, encourages interpretations rooted in creativity, dialogue, summer, culture, movement, and the vibrant spirit of arts & culture. Avoid predominantly black compositions, excessively dark imagery, and highly saturated neon colour schemes. * **Visual Language:** Designers are encouraged to explore broader visual interpretations of the festival through themes such as light, movement, artistic expression, international exchange

1698b241c3d98a9c.description: To contribute to the emergence of works across different disciplines, ADAGP and [Freelens](https://www.freelens.fr/) joined forces in 2021 to create the [Transverse grant](https://www.adagp.fr/fr/soutien-la-creation-artistique/aides-directes-aux-artistes/les-bourses/bourse-transverse). They initially invite a photographer to create a work with an artist from another visual arts discipline, and subsequently, to present it in the form of a book with the support of a publisher.

1698b241c3d98a9c.title: Transverse Exchange Grant

16ba812580ceb7fa.description: IZOLYATSIA Foundation (UA) and Malý Berlín (SK) together with Trans Europe Halles (SE) announces the rolling open call for cultural and arts organisations within the ZMINA: Resilience project, strand 'Support for international showcasing of co-creation projects'. The objective of this call is to support projects that bring artistic and cultural works co-created by Ukrainian and other Creative Europe cultural organisations to wider audiences through public showcasing and presentation events in Ukraine and across other Creative Europe countries. The implementation period is up to 7 months. Funding will be provided to projects featuring co-creations made by partnerships involving at least one organisation from Ukraine and at least one organisation from another Creative Europe country. The projects should maximise the visibility, audience reach, sustainability, and future showcasing potential of these works.

1a9b7e705ed5f77a.description: The Yonge + St. Clair BIA is seeking proposals for art installations as part of the 2027 DesignTO Festival - Canada's largest annual celebration of art and design with over 100 exhibitions and events forming Toronto's design week. The Yonge + St. Clair BIA welcomes artists, architects, designers, fabricators and multidisciplinary creatives to submit ambitious, site-specific installations that activate space, encourage exploration, and create memorable experiences. The Yonge + St. Clair BIA is seeking medium to large-scale installations to be displayed throughout Yonge + St. Clair, reaching thousands of residents, office workers, and visitors. In addition, each installation will receive exposure through DesignTO Festival's marketing channels, guided walking tours, artist talks, and neighbourhood programming. The theme for the Yonge + St Clair neighbourhood this year is: Intersections. Yonge + St. Clair has long been a place where people, ideas and city life intersect. Situated between downtown and uptown Toronto, the neighbourhood brings together residents, businesses, office workers and visitors while continuing to evolve through significant growth and investment. These intersections between communities, disciplines, history, and progress shape the identity of the neighbourhood and the experiences of those who move through it each day. Artists are invited to interpret Intersections through their own creative and critical lens. Proposals may explore themes of convergence, transformation, movement, identity, exchange, and/or the evolving relationship between people and place. The theme is intentionally broad, encouraging innovative responses that activate the selected site. **Duration** 10 days • January 22 - January 31, 2027 **Timeline** September 13, 2026, Submission deadline Late September 2026, Artists selected October 2026, Final project information submitted to DesignTO November 2026, DesignTO Festival announcement January 14-21, 2027, Installation period January 22-31, 2027, Exhibition February 1-2, 2027, De-installation (unless exhibit extended)
1a9b7e705ed5f77a.restrictions: other: This opportunity is open to emerging and established artists, designers, architects, and creative practitioners working in any medium. Preference will be given to applicants based in Toronto and the Greater Toronto Area.
1a9b7e705ed5f77a.title: DesignTO Festival 2027

The Award aims to promote dialogue between contemporary artistic research, sculpture and public space, while enhancing t
1b70bf526bbf6cde.title: Alimondo Ciampi Sculpture Award

1ba9e13093b3b215.description: [**GLEAN**](https://www.gleanportland.com/) is a juried program that gives **five selected artists** from the Portland area (Multnomah, Washington, and Clackamas counties) access to the Metro Central transfer station ("the dump") to glean materials to use to create art. **The GLEAN program will provide studio visits, marketing support, a stipend of $3,000, group critiques with GLEAN artists and partners, and help you work through your creative practice, culminating in an exhibition.** Residents and businesses in the Portland area generate more than 2.4 million tons of waste every year. While we can be proud that we recycle and compost a significant amount, there is an opportunity to do better. GLEAN taps into the creativity of artists to inspire people to think about their consumption habits, the waste they generate, and the resources they throw away. **We reserve one residency position for a student currently enrolled in an art program at a local college or university.** Student applications will be considered separately from other artist applications. GLEAN seeks to hear from artists with a broad range of experiences and perspectives from the many communities in the Portland area. We encourage artists working in a variety of media to apply. You can learn more about past GLEAN artists [**on our website.**](https://www.gleanportland.com/) GLEAN is a partnership between [**Recology**](https://www.recology.com/recology-portland/), an employee-owned integrated resource recovery and recycling company; [**Metro**](https://www.oregonmetro.gov/), the regional government that manages the Portland area's garbage and recycling system; and [**ReClaim It**](https://www.reclaimitpdx.org/), an environmental arts non-profit.
1ba9e13093b3b215.restrictions: other: Applicants must be residents of Multnomah, Washington, or Clackamas county
1ba9e13093b3b215.title: GLEAN 2026/27

1befd5f83cb2046b.description: PQ Publication Cultures **highlights the rich variety of publications** produced about scenography, performance design, and performance space, while also **reflecting on how knowledge in these fields is shared and cultivated**. This includes books and journals, as well as a range of other formats and media, and, importantly, the knowledge communities that sustain and transmit this understanding. An important part of this section is the **PQ Best Publication Award.** Scenographers, theatre designers, and technology experts, scholars, as well as practitioners, create a global knowledge community. Together with publishing houses and institutions, they produce publications about contemporary and historical scenography and performance design. The PQ Publication Cultures program aims at exhibiting and promoting recent publications in the disciplines represented at the Prague Quadrennial, and sharing them with the global community. For PQ 2027, the PQ Publication Cultures program aims to particularly encourage connections within this global community and help the exchange of expert knowledge of scenography and performance design. This is to help the knowledge community, to give learning opportunities to students, and to promote an open culture.

The aim is to facilitate the exchange of expert knowledge, support learning opportunities for students, and promote an open culture in scenography and performance design. **We welcome publications that:** • Cover all scenographic disciplines and genres, including costume, sound, lighting, set, mask, makeup, pr
1befd5f83cb2046b.title: PQ Publication Cultures

1ca3cb59320cc18b.description: Could dreams and nightmares be the potent driving force behind our creative processes, the mysterious catalysts igniting the flame of artistic inspiration? A significant number of artists affirm this belief wholeheartedly. Some find their deepest inspirations enveloped in the essence of dreams, immersing themselves in a blissful trance of creation. This state transcends mere aspiration, becoming a surreal canvas where possibilities bloom endlessly, a place where the mind wanders, seeking the sublime, the ethereal, fostering an insatiable quest to reach heights previously unimagined, somehow, somewhere. On the flip side, many others journey through the chilling domains of nightmares, a voyage marked by relentless internal conflicts and cold sweats that pierce the stillness of the night. These artists find themselves wrestling with the darker fragments of their psyche, exploring into corners where fears manifest and insecurities gnaw persistently. It's a place where conflict brews, giving birth to creations steeped in raw, unfiltered emotion, art that doesn't shy away from exposing the tumultuous storms raging within. It serves as both an exploration and an exorcism of the deep-seated darkness that resides in the corners of the human spirit. Here, the beauty arises from the conflict, the chaos, offering a catharsis that is both profound and unsettling. "I know, I've been there, I am still." This exhibition aims to unearth the profound connections between the subconscious dream world and the pulsating, sometimes harrowing heartbeat of artistic creation, offering a sanctuary for reflection, resonance, and perhaps, revelation. Gallery Space Our gallery is located in one of the most iconic and visited areas in the world- the Tower Bridge district of London. Situated on Tooley Street, the historic link between London Bridge and Tower Bridge, we are just two minutes from both landmarks, four minutes from The Shard, and six minutes from the Tower of London, home to the Royal Crown Jewels. With over 5 million people passing through Tooley Street each month, our gallery has become a celebrated destination. Also- "Our gallery is proud to be one of the 4,000 blue-chip galleries listed on Artsy." Submission Guidelines To apply, email us three images of your work (three different pieces), each with its title, size in cm, medium, price, and a short biography of no more than 150 words. Email submissions should be sent to [boomergallery@gmail.com](mailto:boomergallery@gmail.com). Eligible media include, but are not limited to, paintings, sculptures, photography, installations, prints, textiles, illustrations, digital art, Ai assisted art, poems, etc. Application is free, but a £189 fee (including VAT) applies for each selected artist. This fee covers an extensive suite of benefits: • Printed posters and brochures • Admin support • Graphic designer services • Champagne & caviar at the opening event • Professional photographer to document the event • Hostess, security, and bartender services at the opening • Printing and framing for the artists who opt for that (printing and framing is included in the price). Our exhibition catalogs are state-of-the-art. They present the artist's profile in a magazine-like format, making them valuable beyond the exhibition itself. The catalog will be permanently displayed on our website and continuously circulated by artists, art collectors, and enthusiasts. We facilitate direct connections between artists and collectors and do not charge a commission. Each sale happens directly between the artist and the customer. If you would like us to broker the sale, a 20% VAT will be applied on top of your initial price so please take that into consideration when pricing your works. Printing and Framing Support: If you're an accepted artist facing difficulties shipping your work to us, you can send us photos of your work. We'll print and frame them for you at no additional cost. Rest assured, we strive to match the quality of your original artwork as closely as possible. Frame sizes available: 1\. 32 x 32 cm 2\. 30 x 40 cm A frequent question we receive is: how much should I price my prints if I decide to go with that option? We typically price a framed print at £400, but if you have a different price in mind, please let us know. Remember, printing and framing are included in the participation fee, you don't have to pay anything extra. Important dates: \* Application deadline: 2nd September 2026 \* Artwork delivery date: 10th September 2026 \* Exhibition days: from 11th to the 16th September 2026 \* Opening event on 11th September, from 6:00 to 9:00 pm Event: This is a physical exhibition taking place in our iconic gallery space in the Tower Bridge district, London. Beverages at the event: Champagne, Cocktails, and Caviar. Moreover, we are pleased to permanently include you in our Advisory Program. This program allows us to connect our clients with both emerging and established artists, tailored to their individual preferences, budgets, and styles. By understanding our clients' unique needs, we guide them toward artists whose work aligns with their vision. Since all our exhibitions are thematically curated, and we meticulously catalog every artist we work with, the process of matching clients with the right artists becomes seamless and efficient. If you would like to explore our past exhibitions or browse the works of other artists featured in our catalogs, please visit our website and check the advisory section. Important: When applying, please include "D&M" in the subject line of your email. Good luck to all entrants!
1ca3cb59320cc18b.title: Dreams & Nightmares - Call for Artists

Artists will have the time, space, and inspiration to develop new work in a supportive, immersive environment, with the freedom to focus on their creative process. 24759f4dec13014b.description: Vital Impacts is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization that uses journalism and visual storytelling to amplify and support the work of communities protecting people, wildlife, and habitats around the world. The Vital Impacts Environmental Photography Fellowships and Mentorships support visual storytellers undertaking long-term documentary photography projects that explore environmental and conservation challenges and, importantly, the people and communities working toward solutions. The program has a dual purpose: to provide financial support and mentorship to photographers developing significant bodies of work, while fostering meaningful collaboration with communities and organizations engaged in environmental and wildlife conservation. We are particularly interested in stories that move beyond documenting environmental problems to illuminate the people, communities, and initiatives working toward meaningful solutions.
24759f4dec13014b.restrictions: other: **Who should apply:** Vital Impacts is particularly interested in photographers who have a meaningful, established relationship with the people, places, and issues they are documenting. We believe the strongest environmental stories often emerge from photographers who have taken the time to listen, build trust, understand context, and return to a story over time. We strongly encourage applications from photographers documenting environmental and conservation stories in their own communities. Local photographers bring perspectives, knowledge, access, and relationships that can offer a de
24759f4dec13014b.title: Vital Impacts Environmental Photography Fellowships

253cb90062155f63.description: LIMEN is a two-week residency for artists, filmmakers, writers, and researchers who need real, uninterrupted time - not a weekend, not a rushed sprint, but fourteen days to think, make, and be changed by the place they're in. Based at Casa M, a restored farmhouse in the medieval village of Siddi, Sardinia, residents work independently in their own studio practice while being part of a small group of fellow artists - held in company without losing solitude. Alongside individual work, group sessions rooted in regenerative practices open up memory, both personal and collective, as material for the work itself - what a body carries, what a place holds onto, what gets passed down without ever being named. This material is read through an explicitly political and queer lens, attentive to visibility, erasure, and how power writes itself onto bodies, landscapes, and relationships. The residency is open to conceptual artists, mixed media artists, land artists, visual artists, filmmakers, photographers, researchers, designers, illustrators, educators, community makers, and writers. No prior experience with anthropological or ethnographic methods is required - only curiosity, and a willingness to let two weeks actually change the work. No public showing is required. LIMEN prioritises process over presentation.
253cb90062155f63.place: Siddi, Province of Medio Campidano, Sardinia, Italy
253cb90062155f63.title: Limen - Art Residency

253debb29b2edfeb.description: The Hodder Fellowship will be given to artists and writers of exceptional promise to pursue independent projects at Princeton University during the academic year. Potential Hodder Fellows are composers, choreographers, performance artists, visual artists, writers, translators, or other kinds of artists or humanists who have "much more than ordinary intellectual and literary gifts"; they are selected more "for promise than for performance." Given the strength of the applicant pool, most successful Fellows have published a first book or have similar achievements in their own fields; the Hodder is designed to provide Fellows with the "studious leisure" to undertake significant new work. **General Information** Hodder Fellows spend an academic year with Princeton but no formal teaching is involved. A $93,000 stipend is provided for this 10-month appointment as a Visiting Fellow. Fellowships are not intended to fund work leading to an advanced degree. One need not be a U.S. citizen to apply. Previous recipients of the Princeton Arts Fellowship are not eligible to apply.
253debb29b2edfeb.restrictions: other: We are only accepting applications for the **Program in Dance, Program in Theater and Music Theater, Program in Visual Arts, and the Department of Music** for this cycle.
253debb29b2edfeb.title: The Hodder Fellowship

Art Omi: Artists nurtures deep creative and professional connections in a vibrant, social residency. Artists are provided with a private bedroom in shared living quarters, a private studio, and three meals a day at no cost, but are responsible for their travel and material expenses, unless they are eligible for travel grants as specified in our fellowships guidelines. Each session, two critics/curators are invited to participate as Critics-in-Residence. They both lead discussions, help shape the Visitors program and make individual studio visits throughout the duration of the residency session. **RESIDENCY DATES: Thursday, June 17 - Monday, July 12, 2027**

281dfa62dfd3a284.description: **Grant Types** The Graham Foundation offers two types of grants to individuals: Production and Presentation grants and Research and Development grants. **Production and Presentation:** Production and Presentation grants support projects that advance critical discourse on architecture and related fields and engage public audiences. These grants assist with expenses necessary to realize and publicly present projects such as exhibitions, installations, films, videos, new media and web-based initiatives, publications, and other public programs. Applicants must have a committed producer in place when the Inquiry Form is submitted. A committed producer is an entity that has agreed to produce and/or present the project. Applicants invited to submit a Proposal Form must provide written confirmation of this commitment. Production and Presentation grants must be completed within two years of the project start date. Upon completion, grant recipients must complete a grant report. If funded, grantees should allow sufficient time to meet the grant requirements and acknowledge Graham Foundation support in all published media. **Research and Development:** Research and Development grants support research and development activities that advance a project or idea. Eligible expenses may include travel, archival research, documentation, materials, supplies, and other development costs. Research and Development grants must be completed within one year. Upon completion, grant recipients must complete a grant report. If funded, grantees should allow sufficient time to meet the grant requirements and acknowledge Graham Foundation support in all published media. **For individuals, the Graham Foundation prioritizes projects that:** * Create, develop, and communicate significant ideas about architecture and the designed environment * Support creative, intellectual, and professional growth at a crucial or potentially transformative moment * Take positions, develop forms of expression, and engage debate around architecture and related fields * Bring work into the public realm and reach new or wider audiences * Amplify emerging and underrecognized perspectives in architecture and design, with particular attention to first-time applicants Overall, the Foundation is most interested in projects that align with these priorities, further its mission, and provide critical support at key moments in a project's development. **Criteria for Evaluation** Applications are reviewed holistically, with attention to the project's aims, context, and scale relative to the applicant's experience and resources. In assessing proposals, reviewers consider the following criteria: * Originality: The project demonstrates an innovative and challenging idea; critical, independent thinking; advanced scholarship; a new or experimental approach. * Potential for impact: The project makes a meaningful contribution to discourse in architecture and related fields; expands knowledge; serves as a catalyst for future inquiry; raises awareness of an understudied issue; or broadens the range of subjects, participants, perspectives, and audiences represented. * Feasibility: The project has clear and realistic goals, timeframe, work plan, and budget. * Capacity:The applicant demonstrates the qualifications, knowledge, and ability to carry out the project successfully and has access to the necessary resources beyond the grant request. **How to Apply** The Graham Foundation Grants to Individuals application is an open submission, two-stage process. The review is very competitive and many more applications are received than is possible to fund. Funding decisions at all stages of the review are based on eligibility; alignment of the proposed project to Graham Foundation grant priorities and criteria for evaluation; and availability of grant funds. **Inquiry Form**: Eligible individuals interested in applying for a grant from the Graham Foundation must first submit an Inquiry Form. The Inquiry Form is available on the Foundation's website for each annual open call application period and must be submitted online. **Proposal Form**: After Inquiry Forms are reviewed, applicants whose projects best match the Graham Foundation grant priorities and criteria for evaluation are invited to submit a Proposal Form and supplementary materials. An invitation to submit a Proposal Form does not guarantee eventual funding. Applicants who are not invited to submit a Proposal Form are declined by email. **Award Decision**: Funding recommendations are presented to the Graham Foundation Board of Trustees for consideration. If a grant is awarded, grantees are asked to sign a grant agreement outlining the conditions of the grant, such as annual reporting and acknowledgement of Graham Foundation support within the project. **Calendar for 2027 Grants to Individuals Cycle** FIRST STAGE Inquiry Form Available: July 17, 2026 Inquiry Form Deadline: September 15, 2026, 5 p.m. (Central Time) SECOND STAGE Proposal Form Invitation: December 2026-January 2027 Proposal Form Submission: February 2027 AWARD STAGE Grant Decision Notification: May 31, 2027 Earliest Project Start Date: June 15, 2027
281dfa62dfd3a284.restrictions: other: The Graham Foundation grantmaking programs focus on supporting individuals and organizations in the United States, however, the Foundation also awards grants internationally. **Grants to Individuals:** * Funded projects must include meaningful public dissemination in English. Projects may also be presented in additional languages. * The Graham Foundation does not fund work done in pursuit of an academic degree of any kind. (However, advanced doctoral candidates may be eligible for nomination to the Graham Foundation Carter Manny Award program.) * Individuals may only apply for one grant
281dfa62dfd3a284.title: Grants for Individuals

To live long, things must ever evolve; so must design, to ever last. BKKDW2027 will take place in the Charoenkrung-Talad Noi district and various locations across Bangkok. The Festival welcomes a diverse range of participation formats, including: * Showcases & Exhibitions * Talks * Workshops * Events * Music & Performing Arts * Tours * Markets * Promotions * Projects * Venues

29c1cb3e28fa1ab6.description: Lauched in 2024 to support young emerging artists, the Sixi International Artist-in-Residence Project is committed to facilitating exchanges between artists from different backgrounds and helping them achieve creative breakthroughs and personal growth in their creative work. The Sixi AiR Project will provide living and working space, as well as financial support and other necessary assistance. An apartment in the city center and a loft studio in the outskirts are available for the research and productive demands of artists of different disciplines. Apart from the necessary hardware facilities and staff assistance, we will also help the artists to establish contacts with the local art scene. By the end of the residency period, artists will also have the opportunity to showcase their outcomes in exhibitions. Nanjing is a distinctive Chinese city that combines traditional and contemporary culture, where contemporary art is vibrant in the midst of its rich history. As one of the few local art residency programmes, the Sixi AiR Project hopes to provide artists with the opportunity to engage in dialogue with the city, and to make its contributions to the international cultural exchanges in Nanjing and the diversified development of the art ecology in contemporary China.
29c1cb3e28fa1ab6.restrictions: other: We are calling for artists across all disciplines and cultural backgrounds who are ready to engage in dialogue with the city and achieve creative breakthroughs. **✨ Two Themes for 2027:** 1. Flux and Imprints: Contemporary Echoes of Migration History 2. Folds of Text: Cross-Media Intertextuality and Intervention
29c1cb3e28fa1ab6.title: Sixi International Artist-in-Residence Project

29cbc7fe81e92cd8.description: Would you like to learn to work as a specialist in a technical workshop or in a library with a collection? Would you like to do your own research from within a workshop? Do you live and work in the Netherlands? The Tech Fellowship Programme at the Rijksakademie brings together art and technical expertise. Developed by the Rijksakademie in 2022, it offers artists, makers and designers the chance to work as technical specialists with the aim of preserving traditional craft knowledge and exploring new technologies in the workshops. In this way, we can continue to innovate and respond to contemporary challenges, such as environmental transition and digitalisation. The next edition of the Tech Fellowship Programme runs from January to December 2027.
29cbc7fe81e92cd8.restrictions: other: Please note that we we are recruiting for 6 disciplines, but there is only capacity for 5 tech fellows in 2027. Based on the incoming applications decisions are made regarding the disciplines we include. Please note that this programme is not intended for developing a personal artistic practice in the way the regular Rijksakademie residency is. If you are interested in the residency programme, the next application round opens in January 2027.
29cbc7fe81e92cd8.title: Tech Fellowship Programme 2027

2a7e9dad2f2fc9f9.description: The Artist in Residence (AIR) program offers professional artists in the Austin area an inspiring natural setting in which to explore different mediums and further their artistic development. The 227 acres of Wild Basin Wilderness Preserve are uniquely situated within Austin and reflect the city's personality-at once wild and modern, natural and technologically advanced, protected and developing. Wild Basin hosts two artists per year: in spring and in fall. Artists of all disciplines in the greater Austin area are encouraged to apply. Artists are provided a small budget for materials, supplies, and equipment, a modest stipend, and access to work space within the Wild Basin Creative Research Center and the preserve's trail system. **The Wild Basin Artist in Residence will:** * Donate a piece created during or inspired by their residency to the Wild Basin permanent collection * Present two workshops during the residency: one for adults and one for school-age children * Work on premises at least one day per week * Exhibit works created during the residency at the Wild Basin Visitor Gallery * Be willing to be filmed, photographed or interviewed for Wild Basin promotional purposes * Comply with all policies of Wild Basin while in residence.

2a7e9dad2f2fc9f9.restrictions: other: Artists of all disciplines in the greater Austin area are encouraged to apply.

2b70fb29651f2385.description: Based at Wigwell Lodge, this two-month residency is for artists working with expanded photography and digital practices. This is an opportunity to research, experiment and expand thinking around photography, technology and innovative approaches to image making and visual culture. [The Photographers' Gallery](https://tpg.org.uk/) explores how photography connects, captivates and radically changes our world today. Since 2012, the Gallery's extensive work around digital and new technologies has been pioneering in thinking about photography's relationship to computational culture. The Gallery's programme includes artist commissions, exhibitions, [academic research,](https://thephotographersgallery.org.uk/research) and public events, alongside the online platform [Unthinking Photography](https://unthinking.photography/), which explores photography's increasingly automated and networked life.

Your proposal may respond to one or several of the following themes, or use them simply as a point of departure: * Image-making, celestial fictions and realities * Institutional archives: including The Photographers' Gallery and other archives * Photography's relationship to computational culture * Collective knowledge: human and nonhuman * Deep time * Ideas around civilisations or the un
2b70fb29651f2385.title: Cite the past, sight the stars

2f8664333a961323.description: **Applications are now open for CBA's 2027 Workspace Artist Residency!** Center for Book Arts is a non-profit arts organization dedicated to furthering and uplifting the art of the book. Through residencies, exhibitions, education, and collections, CBA supports artists to explore the book as an artistic medium. Over the past fifty-two years, CBA has worked toward building broad awareness and recognition for artists' books and the artistic practices related to independent bookmaking and publishing. CBA's Workspace Residency invites artists to explore the book as a time-based medium-"a sequence of spaces, each space perceived at a different moment," as described by Ulises Carrión. What new forms of contemporary visual art emerge when the book is approached as an art form? The act of publishing and disseminating ideas through print has long been an essential tool for political engagement. Book arts practices-including printmaking and independent publishing-have historically been central to social and cultural transformation. This year, we invite artists to engage with the book both as a medium and a powerful cultural tool. Center for Book Arts will award up to four New York-based emerging and mid-career artists with space, time, educational and professional development, and financial support to explore the production and exhibition of artists' books and related work through a keyholder residency. The program promotes experimentation in book arts, and artists from all disciplinary backgrounds are encouraged to apply. Our goal is to award residencies to a balanced co-hort of experienced book artists and artists working in other disciplines but with a clear interest in exploring the field. This year's residency period runs for 6 months, from April - September 2027. At the conclusion of the program, artists will present their work and reflect on their residency experience in an artist talk. Residents will have the opportunity to participate in a group exhibition in 2029.
2f8664333a961323.place: 28 W 27th St 3rd fl, New York, NY 10001, USA
2f8664333a961323.restrictions: other: Open to New York-based emerging and mid-career artists.
2f8664333a961323.title: Workspace Artist Residency 2027

31bbc50bbb4b1551.description: SAM Residencies is a museum-run programme committed to supporting the development of innovative artistic and curatorial practices that respond to current global discourses. Developed in line with SAM's vision of engaging local and international artistic communities across a wide range of disciplines, the programme will feature four residency types to support emerging and innovative practices, facilitate collaborations, and widen public understanding of art. The studio-based residencies will be open to artists, curators, art organisations and artist-run spaces, as well as community and education-focused art practitioners. Designed to engage both the art community and the public at large, SAM Residencies will actively involve local communities and the public through a diverse lineup of activities. For the art community, it serves as an incubator for new approaches to artistic and curatorial practices through supporting dialogue within and beyond the field of contemporary art. It offers a platform for artistic experimentation and encourages the exchange of ideas and opportunities for future collaboration, as well as network building. The Residents will also be encouraged to interact with or involve local communities and the public in different ways, through presentations and programmes such as open studio visits, talks, and workshops. Slated to run from June 2027 to December 2028, Cycle 4 is organised around three strands: **Listening/Attuning, Making/Material Cultures and Beyond Human/Interdependence.** **Listening/Attuning** platforms practices that respond critically to the urgencies of our time. **Making/Material Cultures** foregrounds material inquiry and the process of making. **Beyond Human/Interdependence** addresses relationships between humans, technologies, ecologies, and other forms of life, considering how these worlds remain fundamentally interconnected and interdependent. Applicants are invited to interpret these themes in relation to their practice.

3315bc50e17c583a.description: **Position Summary** The Joan Mitchell Catalogue Raisonné project (JMCR) seeks an experienced Researcher to conduct archival and object-based research. The Joan Mitchell Catalogue Raisonné (JMCR) was established by the Joan Mitchell Foundation (JMF) as a limited liability company to research and produce a definitive art historical record documenting the complete oeuvre of paintings on canvas by Joan Mitchell (1925-1992). The catalogue raisonné is currently in the research phase, moving towards readying material for an initial publication. The Researcher's initial focus will be collecting, verifying and updating information and materials related to Joan Mitchell paintings held in Public Collections in the US and abroad. Developing close relationships with these institutions, the Researcher will arrange and conduct painting examinations, coordinate new photography of paintings, manage color-corrections of new and existing photographs of paintings, and consult any relevant, or potentially relevant, public and restricted-access archives. The Researcher will process archival materials and handle queries directed to the Catalogue Raisonné from public institutions. As the project continues, focus will shift to authoring catalogue entries and conducting research (including exams, photography and color correction) on works in private collections. The Researcher is responsible for meticulous data entry (FileMaker, in adherence with the Chicago Manual of Style/JMCR style guide) and the maintenance of complex digital and paper filing systems. Knowledge of 20th-century art history, painting materials and techniques, standard art-handling protocols and prior experience working on a Catalogue Raisonné project (print or digital) are prerequisites. A successful candidate will have excellent communication skills and a great ability to multi-task and prioritize. This position requires independent work as well as collaboration within the JMCR team and the wider Joan Mitchell Foundation. This position is based in the Foundation's New York office with a hybrid (3 days/week in office) schedule. Domestic and international travel is required. **Key Responsibilities Will Include** * Public collection outreach: Cultivate relationships, access paintings, archives and other secondary source materials related to Joan Mitchell in museums and institutions across the US and abroad. * Painting Examinations: Schedule and conduct examinations of Joan Mitchell paintings in public collections worldwide; Document the paintings carefully and thoroughly following the guidelines and format established by the JMCR and dictated by the Exam Form. * Photography: Coordinate with photographers, museum staff, art handlers, storage facilities, etc. to arrange or obtain new photography (recto/verso) of paintings in public collections. This will often require hiring a photographer and sometimes art handlers (in both cases, contracts will need to be negotiated and invoices processed.) * Color Correction: In collaboration with the JMCR's external digital image specialist and JMF's Digital Asset Manager: order, review, annotate and manage photographic proofs of Mitchell's paintings. This requires checking proofs against the paintings themselves to ensure color and material accuracy for publication and filing file proofs and digital files appropriately. * Data processing: Enter data sourced from primary and secondary source materials into the JMCR database (FileMaker) and file in digital and paper files. (Including, but not limited to, information from submission forms, examinations, fact sheets, correspondence, archives, etc.) * Queries: Respond to inquiries from auction houses, galleries, art advisers, and collectors, on behalf of the JMCR, as needed and in collaboration with the Project Manager. * Administrative: Maintain meticulous paper and digital files; track and file expenses; plan travel, collaborate on and adhere to budgets * Strategic planning: Provide the Project Manager with timelines, updates and proposals related to the completion of research, writing, editing and publishing milestones * Research collaboration & knowledge sharing: Collaborate with the Legacy team to strategize and coordinate research, documentation and communication. Report out relevant findings in group meetings.

Several years of significant, scholarly, post-graduate research experience * Familiarity with current catalogue raisonné best practices * Expertise with FileMaker (or similar relational databases); Strong proficiency in d

333ea4759c6e5399.description: The European Cultural Foundation (ECF) was established in 1954 by visionaries such as Denis de Rougemont, Robert Schuman, Hendrik Brugmans and Prince Bernhard of the Netherlands. It was founded on the belief that Europe will not be built by treaties alone. It requires something deeper: a sense that our destinies are connected. For over seventy years, the Foundation has championed the vital role of culture and education in fostering a shared European sense of belonging and solidarity. This commitment has given rise to countless programmes, institutes, campaigns, and collaborations, including its contribution to shaping and implementing the ERASMUS student mobility scheme. The Foundation's capacity to adapt and innovate has uniquely positioned it to respond to, and often anticipate, major transitions in Europe. This legacy is now preserved at the Historical Archives of the European Union (HAEU) in Florence, alongside records of the European Union's main institutions-recognising the Foundation's key role in the European integration process.

35d4457880da0dbe.description: In October 2026, London Art Collective will present ArtEvol 2026: A View from Everywhere, a large-scale international group exhibition bringing together artists working across different cultures, disciplines and lived realities. Through an international Open Call, the exhibition seeks works that reveal how differently the same world can be seen, understood and represented. The title begins with a simple contradiction: no one can see from everywhere. Every perspective is shaped by where we stand, what we have experienced and the structures through which we encounter the world. Rather than searching for a single, universal point of view, the exhibition places different positions alongside one another. Some may overlap; others may disagree or remain unresolved. Together, they form a view that belongs to no single person or place. The exhibition will be presented through a salon-style display within the white cube. Works will appear in close proximity, creating unexpected connections across geography, medium and subject. Painting, sculpture, installation, photography, moving image, digital media and interdisciplinary practices are all welcome. The aim is not to flatten these differences into a shared message, but to allow each work to retain its own position while becoming part of a wider conversation. Curated by Nelson Qin and organised by London Art Collective (LAC), A View from Everywhere will be selected by an international jury of curators, artists, critics and scholars. The jury will consider the clarity of each artist's practice, the strength of the work and what it brings to the exhibition as a whole. The exhibition does not set out to offer a complete picture of the world. Instead, it asks what might become visible when many partial views are brought together.

3a1e824d3e959feb.description: **_Where is the tomorrow we saw yesterday?_** ​spazioSERRA will turn ten in 2027. That's long enough to see a shift in perspective. In recent years, cities have changed, as have the ways of experiencing public spaces, the timeframe of relationships and cultural production. The way art is viewed and the way artists are asked to exist in the present have also changed. And in the meantime, we've changed too. Not only in the way we observe, imagine, and curate, but first and foremost, as people. spazioSERRA was born as a place open to experimentation, and we've grown alongside it. But over time, we've begun to wonder if some of the mechanisms of independent art haven't slowly come to resemble what they were trying to distance themselves from. The deadlines, the need to arrive with already defined ideas, the need to know everything before even starting. We asked ourselves how many possibilities remain when an artistic practice must become immediately exhibitable, performable, and producible. How many attempts disappear because they don't yet have a defined form. And how many ideas, instead, require time, doubt, and error. This is why the 2026 open call for artists was born from a different desire. We're not looking for finished projects. We're not looking for established visions. We'd like to explore practices. Processes. Obsessions. Still-unresolved questions. We're interested in understanding your imprints, what informs your research, what tensions drive it, what possibilities it opens and contradicts within the contemporary scene. Site-specific installations, performances, editorial productions, videos, urban interventions, hybrid collaborations, or still-formless forms: the point is not the format, but the urgency that permeates it. We hope this open call will be the beginning of a space geared toward future projects, open to anyone willing to engage with shared research that can still slow down, change direction, and remain incomplete long enough to transform itself. Because perhaps today the most radical action for a public space dedicated to contemporary art is not to reflect immediacy, but to have the courage to support a still uncertain process.
3a1e824d3e959feb.fee_note: 12 EUR - participation is subject to the payment of a spazioSERRA 2026-2027 membership fee
3a1e824d3e959feb.title: Where is the tomorrow we saw yesterday?

3e3555fd90d38a04.description: Algae, fungi, yeast, natural fibres... grown materials are substances cultivated with living organisms, rather than being extracted from the earth. They are natural, renewable, and biodegradable, whether grown in a lab or on land. The UK's bioeconomy is a government growth priority: the [2025 Modern Industrial Strategy](https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/the-uks-modern-industrial-strategy-2025) names engineering biology as one of six frontier industries, with an ambition for global leadership by 2030. Globally, [the market for mycelium-based materials](https://www.gminsights.com/industry-analysis/mycelium-market) alone is projected to grow from around $3.6 billion today to over $5 billion by 2030, as fashion, construction and packaging industries look for alternatives to plastic, leather and other petrochemical- and animal-derived materials. Yet the UK's own living landscapes for grown materials are themselves under threat. [Seagrass meadows on the west coast of Wales](https://www.projectseagrass.org/blogs/restoring-our-damaged-seagrass-meadows/) have depleted by 92% over the last century, while only around 30,000 hectares remain of Scotland's [temperate rainforests](https://savingscotlandsrainforest.org.uk/). The UK's grown ecosystems are as fragile as they are abundant. **Design Researchers in Residence** is open to designers and researchers from disciplines including but not limited to: biodesign, fashion and textiles, industrial design, architecture, systems and policy research, material innovation, craft or graphic design. We are interested in research that spans the handmade and tactile to the biofabricated and engineered, embedded in natural intelligence. This includes Traditional Ecological Knowledge (TEK), biodesign and biofabrication practices that work with living systems.
3e3555fd90d38a04.restrictions: other: **Design Researchers in Residence: Grown** programme will run from October 2026 to June 2027. The accompanying residency display will be open from June 2027 to September 2027. To be eligible, residents must live and work in the UK, have graduated or set up a design-related business within the last five years, and must have demonstrable experience in carrying out independent research.
3e3555fd90d38a04.title: Design Researchers in Residence

3ed4f87826e9ffe9.description: Public Art Agency Sweden, now a part of Moderna Museet (Museum of Modern Art), is announcing a new opportunity for artists to submit sketch proposals. The new commission concerns a permanent artwork in the Admiralty House's outdoor environment on Skeppsholmen. A collaboration between Public Art Agency Sweden and the National Property Board of Sweden. Skeppsholmen is located in the middle of Stockholm's inlet and is one of the city's most visited places. As part of the National Urban Park, the environment is protected for its significant cultural-historical values. The Admiralty House was built for the Navy's Board of Directors and was completed in 1650. Since its inception, the building has both changed its appearance and served various purposes such as the National Archives, grain warehouses, barracks and offices. In connection with the reconstruction of the Admiralty House and adaptation for the Swedish Institute of International Affairs, a commission is announced for an outdoor public art project. The curatorial vision focuses on Skeppsholmen as a historical landscape shaped by its various connections to the outside world. A place where human movements have manifested themselves in park environments, building history and contemporary cultural exchanges. Through the new artwork, the island's diversity of public art is complemented by a contemporary work that becomes yet another layer of time in the island's history. 3f9bcb6e2c21966e.description: The National Gallery of Iceland is proud to announce an artist residency open call in relation to its CUSP program, a European cooperation project funded through Creative Europe's Culture grant. Artists working in complex media or emerging technologies (e.g. generative AI, custom sensors, sound, software-based, blockchain, physical and digital hybrid, etc) are invited to apply to the residency program. This is the first of four residency stays offered to different artists through the program, one in each of the five participating countries; Iceland, Norway, Czechia and Ukraine, to be followed by two micro residencies in the Netherlands and Iceland. This residency programme brings together artists working time based media and museum professionals, conservators, and technology specialists working to develop the preservation and conservation methodologies required to ensure the long-term endurance of artworks. The artist will meet with a preservation specialist or conservator specializing in time based media art who will conduct an in-depth artist interview aimed at addressing the preservation needs of the medium in which the artist works.
