46444f5aadbb0226.description: OPEN CALL Curators in Flux Founding Edition A 6-Week Hybrid Curatorial Laboratory **Berlin, Germany | February-March 2027** **Applications are now open.** Curators in Flux is a six-week hybrid professional development programme designed for emerging curators who wish to expand their curatorial practice through research, critical dialogue, mentorship, and direct engagement with Berlin's contemporary art ecosystem. Bringing together a small international cohort of **4-6 curators**, the programme combines four weeks of online learning with two immersive weeks in Berlin, culminating in a collective public exhibition. Rather than offering a conventional curatorial course, Curators in Flux creates an experimental learning environment where participants critically examine contemporary curatorial practice while building meaningful professional networks across institutions, artist-run initiatives, and independent cultural spaces. Programme Structure Phase I Online Laboratory **4 Weeks** The online programme creates a collaborative space for research, discussion, and project development. Participants meet several times each week through workshops, lectures, mentoring sessions, and peer discussions. The programme includes: • Curatorial methodology workshops • One-to-one mentoring sessions • Group critiques • Artist and curator talks • Reading seminars • Curatorial writing workshops • Exhibition development • Peer learning sessions Throughout the online phase, participants gradually develop the curatorial concepts that will later be realised collectively during the Berlin residency. Phase II Berlin Laboratory **2 Weeks | Berlin** The second phase takes place entirely in Berlin. Participants immerse themselves in one of Europe's most dynamic contemporary art scenes through an intensive programme of institutional visits, artist studio visits, workshops, and collaborative exhibition production. The programme includes: Institutional Visits Participants will visit leading contemporary art institutions and meet members of their curatorial teams to gain insight into exhibition development, programming, collections, public engagement, and funding structures. Independent Galleries & Artist-Run Spaces Visits to Berlin's independent galleries, project spaces, and artist-run initiatives introduce participants to alternative exhibition models and self-organised cultural practices. Artist Studio Visits Participants will meet Berlin-based artists in their studios, learning about artistic research, production processes, and artist-curator collaboration. Workshops Topics include: • Curating Beyond Institutions • Exhibition Design and Spatial Thinking • Curatorial Writing • Budgeting & Fundraising • Working with Artists • Audience Engagement & Mediation • Accessibility in Curatorial Practice • Producing Exhibitions with Limited Resources Individual Mentoring Each participant receives personalised mentoring sessions focused on their curatorial development and professional goals. Exhibition Production During the final week, participants collaboratively curate and produce a public exhibition in Berlin, presenting projects developed throughout the programme. The exhibition is accompanied by an opening event and public conversation. Who Can Apply? Applications are open to emerging curators from all countries. Applicants should: • Have a minimum of **two years of curatorial experience** • Have previously organised exhibitions, public programmes, or independent curatorial projects • Demonstrate an interest in collaborative and experimental curatorial practice • Be available for the full six-week programme The working language is English. What Participants Receive Participants will receive: • Six-week hybrid curatorial programme • Weekly workshops and seminars • Individual mentoring • Artist and curator talks • Institutional visits • Artist studio visits • Independent gallery and project space visits • Professional networking opportunities • Collective exhibition in Berlin • Certificate of participation Application Requirements Applicants should submit: • CV • Short biography (maximum 200 words) • Letter of motivation (maximum 700 words) • Portfolio of previous curatorial work (maximum 10 pages) • One curatorial research question they would like to explore during the programme (maximum 500 words) Key Dates Applications Open: 05.08.2026 Application Deadline: 04.11.2026 Interviews: 05.11.2026 Selected Participants Announced: 07.11.2026 Programme Begins: February 2027 About Curators in Flux Curators in Flux is an international platform dedicated to supporting the next generation of curators through critical learning, interdisciplinary exchange, and collaborative practice. By connecting institutions, independent organisations, artist-run initiatives, and cultural practitioners, the programme encourages participants to rethink curating as a socially engaged practice capable of building new forms of dialogue, collaboration, and cultural imagination. The Founding Edition marks the beginning of a long-term initiative that will expand into a multi-country hybrid curatorial programme across Central Europe.
46444f5aadbb0226.fee_note: 850 EUR - The participation fee covers the educational component of the programme, including all workshops, seminars, artist talks
46444f5aadbb0226.title: Curators in Flux

4846c387f3dead1a.description: The Napa Lighted Art Festival is a celebration of creative arts, technology, and lights. The Napa Lighted Art Festival is a free, open-air festival with the nighttime backdrop of downtown Napa. It is open to all members of the public and will attract admirers from near and far. Currently in its 8th edition, the festival supports innovative techniques using light and light technologies as a growing art medium. Both artists and artist groups are encouraged to apply to have an installation featured at the Napa Lighted Art Festival. For the 2026 Festival, the curatorial team will select approximately 10 installations to receive a stipend between $2,000-$10,000. Artists interested in submitting should consider both the audience and the outdoor environment of the festival when proposing a project. Each artwork of the Napa Lighted Art Festival will be open and operational for all festival hours for each of the nights. The spirit of the Napa Lighted Art Festival embodies the following core concepts: * Innovative * Contemporary * Uplifting * Inspiring * Imaginative The festival supports innovative techniques using light and light technologies as a growing art medium. **Light itself in any form should be the actual artwork, and we require that the role of light be essential to your concept.** We are not looking for artworks where light is used only to illuminate it. We also strongly encourage new technologies and innovative use of light. As well as new ideas for artworks, we are open to receiving proposals to exhibit existing works, provided they meet the festival themes and criteria. Artwork could include any of the following genres and/or technology: light sculptures, light art, video art, 3D video mapping projections, LED, fiber optics, custom gobo designs, interactive works, lasers etc. **General Festival Information** _Festival Dates:_ January 17th - February 15th, 2026 _Festival Times:_ Sunday-Thursday 6:00-9:00 p.m. and Friday-Saturday 6:00-10:00 p.m. _Location:_ Various sites and buildings in the Napa Downtown Area **Napa Lighted Art Festival** The Napa Lighted Art Festival started in 2017 and the festival had the 7th exhibition in 2025. The festival's attendance is approximately 70,000. In addition to the art installations, past festivals have included the iconic Napa Valley hot air balloons called "Night Bloom" that lit up the Oxbow Commons and a community driven Lantern Parade where everyone gets to make their own lighted art. The festival has included artist meet and greet experiences, educational or historical tours, and musical performances. The festival is free and open to the public. **Artwork Selection Criteria** **_Construction_**_:_ All works at Napa Lighted Art Festival are staged in the public spaces for an extended time and this requires rigid constructions. At times, the weather in Napa during the winter can vary from year to year. Napa can be stormy, wet and cold, so the technical feasibility, rigidity and durability of your concept is of utmost importance. A construction overview of durability is required with your submission. For some structures or sculptures, it will be required to provide stamped engineering drawings. **_Sound_**_:_ The use of sound is encouraged when possible with projection mapping pieces. The soundtrack should be submitted with the correlating visuals. **_Lighting:_** All sculptures or physical artwork must be able to be powered the entire time or provide a timer to self-turn-on every evening by 6pm. The festival staff will not manually turn on any installation. **_Period_**_:_ Digital artwork must be available and uploaded to the provide Drop Box folder by Monday December 8, 2025. Sculptures or any physical art for the festival needs to arrive and be installed no later than January 10, 2026 (and deinstalled no later than February 28, 2026). **_Visitor Experience_**_:_ Please keep in mind that your work may be positioned in pedestrian zones, sidewalks, parking lots, or perhaps in a plaza or park-like setting. Visitors will be able to experience your artwork from approximately 50-100 feet for installations such as projection artwork on buildings or be able to touch it for physical artwork. They will expect to be amazed as they walk from exhibit to exhibit but also spend time at each installation. Community members and visitors should enjoy sharing their experience with others and/or have a deeper personal understanding about the relationship between light, art and the festival's core concepts & theme. **_Location_**_:_ There are different types of locations along the festival art walk route. Your work will be positioned in a pedestrian zone adjacent to a private or public building, mainly along the downtown corridor. The potential locations are included but are subject to change. The artist may suggest a location for the artwork upon submission; however, the curatorial team will make the final decision in favor of the entire visitor experience of the festival route. **_Technical Limitations_**_:_ The artist will be provided with a description of the technical limitations for each site. The festival strives to push the boundaries of technology through art. However, the safety and well-being of the participants and property are of the highest importance. Please note there are safety considerations as people will be moving through and around the art installation. There may be limitations due to building code and other factors. Therefore, based on budget and physical location, there may be limitations to achieve technical realization. In some cases, a different approach may be needed or recommended in consultation with the artist. **_Curatorial Team:_** Curatorial team consisting of City of Napa staff and possible consultants conducting the initial review of the submissions to ensure the applications are complete as well as meet the artistic and technical requirements For installations at private property sites, the property owners often are involved in the final selection of the installations. The curatorial team will select artworks that together form a coherent and harmonious exhibition based upon the goals and core concepts for the festival.
4846c387f3dead1a.restrictions: other: **Applications Review Process:** All submissions will be reviewed by the curatorial team to assess compliance with the requirements, technical feasibility and overall quality of the submission. The curatorial team will call the artist to get more information or clarification if needed. The curatorial team will then review the artworks for the festival based on both the artistic impact of the work, the creativity of the concept, and the alignment with the festival's core concepts and selection criteria list below. The curatorial team will also consider whether a submission fits into the
4846c387f3dead1a.title: Napa Lighted Art Festival 2026

4d0fe7af6c584355.description: A Space Gallery (Brooklyn, NY) is excited to announce that our Fall 2026 Open Call for Artist Solo Exhibition is now open for submissions. Selected solo exhibitions will take place during Fall 2026, with final scheduling determined in collaboration with each selected artist based on the nature of the work and the gallery's programming calendar. ​We are especially interested in supporting underrepresented artists, projects that engage the gallery space in thoughtful or unexpected ways, and works that may not easily fit within the framework of a traditional commercial gallery. We welcome submissions from artists of all educational backgrounds and career stages, and we encourage applications from artists based both across the United States and internationally. Artists selected for a solo exhibition will work closely with A Space Gallery's curatorial team to develop and prepare their exhibition. **​Exhibition and Delivery Requirements:** * Work must arrive by the exhibition installation date and must be installed by the artist. A Space Gallery staff member will assist the artist. * A label must be attached to the back/bottom of each work with the **name, title, medium, and price.** * Work must be presented in a manner appropriate to the artwork and be equipped for presentation. * If work is shipped, include a prepaid return shipping label with your package. * No work that was not originally selected by or discussed with A Space Gallery will be displayed.​
4d0fe7af6c584355.title: Solo Exhibition at A Space Gallery in Fall 2026

4d65f10b2b824e9f.description: With a flexible, often shorter timeframe of one to six months, the Individual Fellowship gives artists, scholars, and arts professionals from Asia and the U.S. the opportunity to pursue research, self-directed exploration and cultural immersion experiences in a new or less familiar environment, fostering peer-to-peer dialogue, collaboration, and knowledge-sharing. An Individual Fellowship is not a residency to produce new work, a fund to attend or participate in a single conference or event (i.e. not a travel grant), or an individual's public relations tour. Rather, Individual Fellows explore questions and activities that enable and promote cultural immersion. These experiences and relationships lead to invaluable creative inspiration, collaborative opportunities, and a more global and nuanced perspective. **What does the Individual Fellowship offer?** **Freedom to Explore:** This fellowship supports travel to countries, territories, or regions that are new or less familiar to applicants, enabling them to pursue self-designed research and cultural exchange activities. Examples of past Individual Fellow activities include: * Interviewing or meeting professionals and other stakeholders who can provide relevant expertise * Visiting institutions (e.g., studios, museums, galleries, theaters, libraries) or attending events (e.g., exhibitions, performances, lectures, film screenings) aligned with their research and exchange goals * Participating in workshops, symposia, or discussions that advance the exchange of knowledge, ideas, and practices and connects fellows with new communities * Conducting archival research **Individualized Support:** ACC offers guidance to enhance proposed activities, expand access to arts and culture, and deepen cultural exchange experiences. Support may include logistical or research advice, introductions to alumni or professionals, invitations to local events, and visa assistance for U.S. travel. ACC offices are in New York, Hong Kong SAR, Japan, the Philippines, and Taiwan, so some services may be limited depending on the location of the fellowship. **Proposals should be feasible even without extensive ACC support.** **Fellowship Travel Dates and Duration** * **All ACC fellowship travel must occur within the grant period:** August 1, 2027 - December 31, 2028. * **Individual Fellowships must have a duration of at least one month, but no more than six months.** * **ACC believes that cultural exchange and immersion is enhanced when Individual Fellows spend a greater period of time (at least two months, preferably) exploring one place**, rather than visiting multiple countries, territories, or regions for a shorter period. It is also important to consider logistical challenges and/or restrictions related to traveling to multiple countries, territories, or regions during a fellowship. * **Applicants pursuing a fellowship in the U.S. must plan to spend at least 30 consecutive days in the country.** * Fellowships in the U.S. cannot commence prior to October 1, 2027, due to the time needed to administer J-1 visas (see "Visa Requirements" section below). * **Applicants pursuing a fellowship in Asia must propose at least 30 cumulative (total) days in the region.** * If a visa does not allow travel for more than 30 consecutive days, applicants may propose multiple trips totaling at least 30 days. Each trip must be **at least 14 consecutive days**, with no more than 14 days between trips. * Applicants proposing multiple shorter trips to the same destination should explain how they will **fully engage with the local culture** despite these breaks. * Applicants proposing a single brief trip (e.g., three weeks) as part of a multi-destination itinerary should provide a **rationale** for the short duration (e.g. three weeks in China after two months in Japan) * **ACC strongly discourages travel outside the proposed destinations during the fellowship**, with the exception of medical and family emergencies (see also the "Visa Requirements" section below). Individual Fellows who have essential and unavoidable career-related travel needs must submit a "Change in Proposed Grant Activity" Form seeking ACC's approval at least 60 days before the fellowship start date.

Eligible applications must meet the following requirements: * **Eligible Activities:** ACC fellowship and grant funding is strictly limited to supporting activities related to cultural exchange and immersive experiences. ACC does not fund production or promotional activities, including activities intended to directly or indirectly produce, exhibit, or perform a specific, predetermined work product. 4d90dbb2d2b5b873.description: Since 2014, The Image Centre has offered a variety of fellowships for research related to photography. Research fellows have the opportunity to study select areas of The Image Centre's photography collections first-hand. **In 2027, The Image Centre will offer six competitive fellowships for research related to photography.** All applicants are encouraged to read the following guidelines closely and apply to the appropriate fellowship, based on their subject of study and eligibility. Artists and other scholars seeking to conduct artistic research in the collections, are encouraged to apply for the Howard Tanenbaum Fellowship exclusively. Past winners of IMC Fellowships may not reapply for five years following submission of their previous final report. The IMC will not consider incomplete applications or blanket applications for multiple fellowships; applicants will only be considered for fellowships for which they are eligible. All fellowships are available to Canadian and international applicants. **The IMC/AMC Postdoctoral Fellowship** Jointly supported by the IMC and the Archive of Modern Conflict (AMC), this fellowship invites scholars to undertake research across two internationally significant photography collections. This full-time opportunity requires that the fellow will be in-residence in Toronto, carrying out sustained research in the collections during a one-year period, from July 1, 2027-June 30, 2028. The fellowship includes an annual salary of $70,000 (CAD) and benefits, and a generous research stipend to support research in London, UK. Candidates **must hold** a PhD at the time of application. For more information about the IMC/AMC Postdoctoral Fellowship, including how to apply, please visit: [www.torontomu.ca/careers/research-staff-opportunities/imc-amc-postdoctoral-fellowship-july-8-2026/](https://www.torontomu.ca/careers/research-staff-opportunities/imc-amc-postdoctoral-fellowship-july-8-2026/) **The Nadir Mohamed Postdoctoral Fellowship** This fellowship includes a $10,000 (CAD) stipend for travel, research, and other related expenses. Candidates must hold a PhD degree. Candidates' research should utilise the collections and resources of The Image Centre and/or Toronto Metropolitan University Archives and Special Collections. The fellow will be expected to carry out their research on-site for a minimum of one (1) to a maximum of three (3) months, between February 15 and December 15, 2027. **The Penny Rubinoff Fellowship** This fellowship includes a $5,000 (CAD) stipend for travel, research, and other related expenses. Candidates must hold a master's degree; this includes PhD students or candidates, and excludes applicants who hold a PhD or are postdoctoral researchers. Candidates' research should utilise the collections and resources of The Image Centre and/or Toronto Metropolitan University Archives and Special Collections. The fellow will be expected to carry out their research on-site for a minimum of two (2) to a maximum of six (6) weeks, between February 15 and December 15, 2027. **The Elaine Ling Fellowship** This fellowship includes a $4,000 (CAD) stipend for travel, research, and other related expenses. Candidates must have recently completed a master's degree, or be working toward its completion. Students who are currently enrolled in a doctoral program, hold a PhD or are postdoctoral researchers are ineligible. Candidates' research should utilise the collections and resources of The Image Centre and/or Toronto Metropolitan University Archives and Special Collections. The fellow will be expected to carry out their research on-site for a minimum of one (1) to a maximum of four (4) weeks, between February 15 and December 15, 2027. **The Howard Tanenbaum Fellowship for Artistic Research** This fellowship includes a $4,000 (CAD) stipend for travel, research, and other related expenses but does not include access to production facilities such as printing labs and darkrooms. Candidates may hold any level of education, and/or be independent artists with relevant experience and demonstrated interests. Candidates' research should utilise the collections and resources of The Image Centre and/or Toronto Metropolitan University Archives and Special Collections in support of their artistic practice. They should demonstrate awareness of copyright considerations in their use of historical images; they should propose creative methodologies and outputs. The fellow will be expected to carry out their research on-site for a minimum of one (1) to a maximum of four (4) weeks, between February 15 and December 15, 2027. **The Wendy Snyder MacNeil Research Fellowship** This Fellowship includes a $4,000 (CAD) stipend for travel, research and other related expenses but does not include access to production facilities such as printing labs and darkrooms. Candidates should possess or be working towards at least an undergraduate degree, and/or be photo-based artists. Candidates' research should utilise the collections and resources of The Image Centre and/or Toronto Metropolitan University Archives and Special Collections to support new perspectives on the work of women photographers, including Wendy Snyder MacNeil. The fellow will be expected to carry out research onsite for a minimum of one (1) to a maximum of four (4) weeks, between February 15 and December 15, 2027. This fellowship was established in memory of photographer and filmmaker Wendy Snyder MacNeil (1943-2016). Best known for her documentation of Boston's Haymarket district, her use of vernacular imagery in forms of extended portraiture, and her later, larger-scale work in platinum/palladium, MacNeil was also an avid student of history and an educator deeply interested in the ways photographic images convey a sense of an individual, a family, or a group of people drawn together by culture or circumstance. All of her major projects are part of The Image Centre which holds the entirety of MacNeil's personal photographic archive.

Dates of residency will be established in dialogue with the IMC's staff. Research fellows must agree to abide to regulations as directed by Toronto Metropolitan University, The Image Centre, and the Ministry of Health for the province of Ontario. Fellows are expected to pay the cost of travel and accommodation in Toronto. The stipend awarded with the fellowship is intended to offset these costs. Fellows without Canadian citizenship are r

52228e5b0bea0aed.description: **_Making Policy Public_** is an annual program where advocates, organizers, graphic designers, and illustrators collaborate with CUP to create an accessible print resource that uses art and design to explain a public policy, process, system, or social justice issue. Directly impacted community members also collaborate on projects through feedback sessions organized by the advocate with support from CUP. The knowledge of communities with lived experience is a critical part of collaborations and supports projects that are well-informed, meaningful, and effective. Since 2009, projects have supported over 500,000 New Yorkers to assert their rights, benefit from social services, and organize to create more just and equitable systems. Projects have supported greater justice and equity for marginalized communities across issues of housing, community development, labor, environment and climate, immigration, incarceration, education, healthcare, and language access. **Projects have supported advocacy and organizing by:** * oversee equitable and just implementation of public policies and programs * train communities on their rights and ways to assert their power * organize for concrete neighborhood improvements * increase the number of people who benefit from services and programs * increase public participation in public processes and issues * strengthen community-centered solutions and policies _Making Policy Public_ is a program of [**The Center for Urban Pedagogy (CUP)**](http://welcometocup.org) - a nonprofit organization that uses the power of art and design to increase meaningful civic engagement, in partnership with marginalized communities. Since 2001, CUP has worked with over 150 community organizations and 325 visual artists and designers to create accessible community education about the public policies, processes, and systems that affect New York City communities. **Selection Process** * **September - Application Review:** CUP staff review applications for eligibility and share a final list of applications with the jury to review. * **October - Jury Review:** Jury members review applications individually and then come together for a jury meeting in late October. The jury selects the finalists who will be interviewed by CUP staff. * **Mid November - Finalist Interviews:** Finalists are interviewed by CUP staff. Interviews are 1 hour and will take place between November 9-18. * **Early December - Selection Notification:** CUP notifies selected finalists. * **January** **-** **Partner Orientation**: All selected partners come together Wednesday, January 20 to kick off _Making Policy Public_ with an orientation at CUP's office in Gowanus. **How Does _Making Policy Public_ Work?** **Open Call and Selection** Advocates and designers respond to CUP's annual open call for Making Policy Public. A jury of designers and advocates use criteria to select up to four community organizations' and four designers/design teams. Selected community organizations participate at no cost to their organization. Selected designers receive a $5,000 or $8,000 honorarium (depending on the scope of the project they are selected to work on)-paid in three installments. **Orientation and Kick Offs** Selected community partners and designers attend a partner orientation on January 20, 2027. Two of the four selected projects kick off at the end of January 2027 and the other two kick off in March 2027. **Collaboration and Community Engagement** Each project team collaborates over **7-12 months**, depending on the scope and format of the project. CUP facilitates the collaborations, bringing experience in project management, community engagement, understanding complex policies, art direction, language access, and writing in plain language. Advocates and organizers bring their deep knowledge of the issues impacting communities. Directly impacted community members participate in feedback sessions, to shape the project with their lived experience. Designers and illustrators bring their visual skills, creativity, and commitment to using their skills to uplift communities. Together, we create a project that supports community-centered advocacy, organizing, and participation. **Production and Launch** Advocates receive 1,000 free copies of the final project to distribute directly to their communities and networks, Advocates must organize a public launch event within 3 months of printing to get the final resource out into communities. The launch event can be connected to the work you're already doing, like an existing training, committee meeting, or public event **_Making Policy Public_ Project Schedule** **January 2027:** Partner Orientation on January 20th; 1st round of collaborations kickoff **February 2027:** Anti-oppression, bias in visual design, and receiving feedback trainings **March 2027:** 2nd round of collaborations kickoff **May 2027:** Managing deliverables training **July 2027:** Cohort Gathering to discuss and reflect on projects. **By March 2028:** Projects launch through a project-specific public event

52228e5b0bea0aed.title: Making Policy Public Fellowship 2026

5424e77164dc712d.description: Founded in 1962 by Edward Albee - after proceeds from his play _Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?_ proved abundant-the Edward F. Albee Foundation has maintained the William Flanagan Memorial Creative Persons Center (aka "The Barn") in Montauk, Long Island, for nearly 60 years. The Center exists to serve writers and visual artists from all walks of life by providing uninterrupted time and space to work. **Location & Environment** Located about two miles from downtown Montauk and the Atlantic Ocean, "The Barn" sits on a secluded knoll offering privacy and a peaceful atmosphere. Residents are expected to work seriously and to support a respectful, focused environment for fellow artists. The environment is simple and communal. Residents share responsibility for maintaining the space and preserving its peaceful atmosphere. **Residency Structure** The Center operates nearly year-round and accommodates four creative people at a time. Residencies are offered for full calendar months, and applications are accepted twice annually. The August/September application period is for residencies in January-June; the January/February application period is for residencies in July-November. The Barn is closed every December.
5424e77164dc712d.restrictions: other: Using only talent and need as criteria, the Foundation invites writers and visual artists from all backgrounds to apply.
5424e77164dc712d.title: Winter/Spring Residency 2027

54c6d296d8345aa3.description: The Humboldt Gymnasium will be expanded at its current location with an addition along the Augustinerhof courtyard, and the existing extension will be raised by one story. Simultaneously, the existing building will undergo comprehensive renovation in certain areas. The architectural concept is based on a balanced combination of traditional and contemporary materials and construction methods, on a harmonious interplay of robustness and naturalness. As part of this construction project, an artwork is to be designed for the centrally located stairwell of the extension. The constant movement within the stairwell creates continuously changing viewpoints and perspectives, so that the art is not confined to a fixed vantage point but can be experienced in motion. The artwork should enhance the school's expansion, while simultaneously addressing and openly interpreting the school's values ​​such as integration, diversity, the evolution of knowledge, the future and transformation, curiosity and critical thinking, and personal responsibility, and engaging in a dialogue with the architecture and the distinctive exposed concrete surfaces of the stairwell.

5bd2aa1f9468be11.description: The Openshaw Artist-in-Residence Program provide a supportive atmosphere for emerging artists in a collective setting, giving them an opportunity to develop their voice and contribute to the community at Maryland Hall. The residency offers studio space, support in the form of a materials stipend, and basic marketing around the exhibition. At the end of the residency, Openshaw AIRs will present a solo show in the Openshaw Balcony Gallery. **Program Goals and Objectives** * To provide time and space for artists to investigate ideas while working towards a collection or series to be presented in the Openshaw Balcony Gallery * To maintain and enhance the quality and diversity of the creative services offered by Maryland Hall and to host a diverse group of artists. * To foster creativity by providing solitude and community through affordable, subsidized studio space, with mutual trust that the artist will use the opportunity to move their work forward. * To enrich and stimulate the community through activities offered by Artists-in-Residence such as workshops, demonstrations, open studio events, lectures, and performances. * To expand the audience base of Maryland Hall and to welcome young artists into our community. **Program Description** The Openshaw AIR program consists of one artist studio which rotates new artists every two months. During the residency, the visual artist will work on a collection or series which they will present in the Openshaw Balcony Gallery at the end of the residency. The material stipend provided to each artist is $500 and can be used for materials and supplies needed for the artist's exhibit. Upon completion of the residency, the AIR will curate and install their work, which will remain up for two months. Building hours during which the studios can be used are Monday - Friday 8 am - 11 pm, Saturday 8 am - 5 pm. Maryland Hall is committed to making the space available to artists who are passionate to pursue their work on a consistent basis. AIRs are encouraged to regularly use the studio space to create original work. It is expected that artists use their studio for a minimum of 15-20 hours per week. Studios are not to be used as office space. After the residency, artists can apply for the general AIR program if there is availability. **Residencies January through March 2027**
5bd2aa1f9468be11.restrictions: other: Artists are required to be residing in the DC-Maryland-Virginia area. Commercial artists and non-profits arts groups are not eligible for the residency. While the program operates on the honor system, if an AIR should find that they are not able to use their studio due to life changes etc., this request this be addressed with Maryland Hall staff immediately.

5cd7366b020456ea.description: A Juried Exhibition on James Baldwin's proposition for Truth February 5 through March 27, 2027 **Exhibition Title:** _As Much Truth as One Can Bear_ **Entry Fee:** $20 **Type:** Juried Exhibition **Prize Money:** Up to $3500 in awards. **The Arts Center in Orange, VA, is accepting submissions from artists of African American heritage for its upcoming Juried Exhibition centered on James Baldwin's essay and proposition about Truth, As Much Truth as One Can Bear. Up to $3500 in prize money will be awarded.** **Theme:** Truth, identity, justice, memory, emotional endurance, and social reality. _As Much Truth as One Can Bear_ takes its conceptual grounding from James Baldwin's assertion that truth is not simply known-it is endured. This exhibition invites artists of African American heritage to explore the limits of perception, the weight of lived experience, and the tension between what is revealed and what is resisted. Truth, in this context, is not singular or stable. It is layered, emotional, historical, and often uncomfortable. Artists in this exhibition are not asked to illustrate Baldwin, interpret his biography, or translate his texts into visual form. Instead, they are asked to enter into a condition of engagement-where their work must reckon with what it means to face something directly, without avoidance or resolution. The works in this juried exhibition engage with identity, race, memory, justice, love, and survival. Some works confront directly; others unfold quietly. Together, they create a space where viewers are asked not only to observe, but to reckon. **We Are Seeking Work That:** * Explores personal or collective truths * Engages with visibility, silence, or resistance * Responds to cultural, political, or emotional realities * Challenges viewers to reflect or reconsider **Eligibility:** Open to emerging and established artists of African American heritage, including students. Must be 18 to enter. There will be a Best in Show award of $650.00, and 1st Prize - $400, 2nd Prize - $300, 3rd Prize - $200, and three Juror's Choice winners of $150/each **Accepted Media:** Painting, drawing, photography, sculpture, mixed media, installation, digital work, text-based work, video, textile and interdisciplinary practices **Submission Guidelines** * 5-10 images or time-based samples of recent work * Artist statement (300-500 words) * CV or short biography highlighting continued practice * Optional reflection on time in your work * $20 submission fee - paid on website * Email submissions on [artscenterinorange.com](http://artscenterinorange.com) under Calls, to email [submissions@artscenterinorange.com](mailto:submissions@artscenterinorange.com) * Put "As Much Truth As One Can Bear" In the subject line. * Deadline for submissions: October 1, 2026 **Selection Criteria:** * Conceptual strength * Originality * Relevance to theme * Technical quality * Emotional impact **WHY THIS SHOW** We are living in a time of constant information but limited reflection. This exhibition creates space to slow down and engage deeply. The Art Center believes that art provides a way to process complex truths beyond debate and that communities benefit from shared spaces for dialogue and reflection. In addition, young people need platforms to express what they see in the world. James Baldwin's work remains urgent, bridging generations and connecting historical truths to contemporary realities. Today, the question is no longer _what is truth?_ but _what are we willing to face?_ To experience this exhibition is to participate in an act of witnessing. The viewer is not outside the work-they are implicated in it. If we can only bear so much truth at once, then this exhibition becomes a collective space to expand that capacity.
5cd7366b020456ea.restrictions: other: Open to emerging and established artists of African American heritage, including students. Must be 18 to enter.
5cd7366b020456ea.title: As Much Truth as One Can Bear

5f2a65f10f6504d7.description: PhotoVogue's Regional Open Call invites photographers and video makers from West Asia and North Africa and their diaspora to bring forward their perspectives, celebrating image-making as a space of expression, resilience, and cultural dialogue, and offering global visibility to their work. **WANA Panorama** is PhotoVogue's regional initiative to champion the plurality of voices from WANA, moving beyond monolithic narratives to showcase the region's complexity, resilience, and diverse visual languages. At a time of profound transformation across the region, this open call aims to create space for artists to represent themselves and their communities on their own terms, fostering visibility, nuance, and connection through image-making. WANA is not a monolithic space. It is shaped by a wide range of cultures, histories, and social realities, as well as by ongoing transformations and forms of resilience. For this reason, this open call does not aim to define the region, but to create a platform where artists can represent themselves, their communities, and their environments on their own terms. We are particularly interested in works that reflect the diversity of lived experience, whether through intimate storytelling, explorations of identity and belonging, engagements with fashion and visual culture, or reflections on social, political, and environmental realities. At the same time, the open call welcomes practices that move beyond representation, embracing experimentation, abstraction, and new visual forms.
5f2a65f10f6504d7.restrictions: other: **We invite photographers and video makers from West Asia and North Africa (WANA), as well as those from the diaspora who maintain a meaningful connection to the region.** Across all genres, from fashion to documentary, portraiture, fine art, and beyond, we are looking for work that reflects the richness, complexity, and plurality of experiences across the region, as well as practices that push visual language in new and unexpected directions.
5f2a65f10f6504d7.title: PHOTOVOGUE'S REGIONAL OPEN CALL: WANA Panorama

61704f6caa5ac293.description: These laboratory-format residencies invite artists, writers, and researchers from diverse disciplines to explore walking as an artistic and research methodology through an intensive process of collective work situated within the landscape of Montserrat. The program proposes a sustained period of immersion in which walking is understood as a generative practice for perceiving, mapping, and narrating place through embodied experience. Over several weeks, participants will develop an ongoing process of research, exchange, and production, combining sensory exploration, ecological observation, site-responsive creation, and reflective practices. The laboratory is structured as a trajectory that moves through storytelling, the body, processes of thought, ecological narratives, and food, culminating in a phase of synthesis and formalization of the work developed. This process unfolds through proposals involving group movement, writing, reading, sound, video, visual practices, and feedback sessions grounded in conversation. The landscape of Montserrat functions as both terrain and collaborator: a living archive that is traversed, interpreted, and collectively reimagined through shared movement. While Can Serrat and its collaborators propose a semi-structured framework, the laboratory is built through active participation, inviting participants to share methods, approaches, and working processes within a context of collective experimentation. **PROGRAM STRUCTURE** The program is organized into two main phases, each divided into three weeks focused on different themes, and is conceived as a progressive process combining autonomous units and a full trajectory. Weeks 1 and 2 can be taken independently as intensive modules. The full trajectory (weeks 1 to 3) allows for the development of a continuous process of research, exchange, and production, and constitutes the recommended form of participation. Week 3 is conceived as a phase of synthesis and formalization and is not available as an independent module. **PROGRAM I - PALIMPSESTS (Weeks I-III)** Focus: storytelling, sensory relationship with the landscape, and the connection between movement and thought. Week I (January 10-16) - Storytelling, mapping, and territory Exploration of Montserrat as a stratified territory shaped by legends and historical and personal narratives. Work with storytelling, mapping exercises, and collective reflection sessions using sound, video, and writing. Sarah Goodchild Robb will lead a walk and propose exercises to connect with local legends and personal narratives. Week II (January 18-23) - Climate, body, and sensory landscapes A sensory approach to place, exploring how climate, atmosphere, and the body shape the perception of landscape. A guest practitioner from the somatic field will guide a series of exercises to connect with the environment. Week III (January 25-30) - Walking and thinking Walking as a mode of thought. This phase focuses on the articulation between embodied experience and conceptual processes, oriented toward the formalization and development of individual or collective materials. Sophie Blais will lead a session focused on thinking processes. **PROGRAM II - PHOTOSYNTHESIS (Weeks IV-VI)** Focus: ecological relations, transformation, local plants, food, and collective creation. Week IV (February 1-6) - Ecological histories Exploration of the ecological histories of Montserrat, considering the impact of tourism and climate change through botanical walks and material practices. A local practitioner will guide a plant identification walk. Week V (February 8-13) - Gathering, cultivating, and feeding the landscape Engagement with the landscape through practices of foraging, cultivation, and cooking. Work around food, composting, and ecological cycles, designing and preparing shared meals. Dialogue with Can Serrat's Gardening Project. Week VI (February 15-20) - Synthesis and creation A phase dedicated to integrating experiences and developing individual or collective outcomes.
61704f6caa5ac293.restrictions: other: **WHO CAN APPLY** People of any background and age (minors with authorization). It is not necessary to be an artist or writer. Individual, duo, or collective applications are accepted.
61704f6caa5ac293.title: Walking Practices Laboratory 2027

6795e8999d6fb996.description: Miami International Fine Arts, MIFA, invites curators, art researchers, art writers, cultural producers, and creative professionals with curatorial experience to apply to the MIFA Curators-in-Residence Program 2027. MIFA is a multidisciplinary arts center located between Doral and Miami Springs. Its programming integrates arts education, artist residencies, exhibitions, printmaking, performing arts, music, poetry, and interdisciplinary projects. The Curators-in-Residence Program seeks to strengthen emerging curatorial voices, support the professional development of artists, and build a rigorous and diverse exhibition program connected to the cultural context of South Florida. For the 2027 edition, MIFA will select up to five curators who will collaborate with the Artistic Director in evaluating exhibition proposals, mentoring participating artists, and developing exhibitions throughout the institution. **The program aims to:** * Strengthen the professional practices of emerging and mid-career curators. * Create opportunities for the development of independent curatorial research. * Support artists in the conceptualization, editing, and public presentation of their bodies of work. * Promote dialogue among artists, curators, researchers, educators, and communities. * Consolidate a diverse, critical, and professionally developed exhibition program at MIFA throughout 2027. The Curators-in-Residence will participate actively in the development of MIFA's 2027 exhibition calendar and will be expected to fulfill the following responsibilities: **Exhibition Project Selection** * Participate in the review of applications submitted through the MIFA 2027 Open Call for Exhibition Projects. * Evaluate proposals using a shared assessment rubric established by the Artistic Director. * Participate in committee deliberations and interviews with shortlisted artists and collectives. * Identify projects that are relevant to MIFA's different galleries, audiences, and areas of research. * Provide clear, thoughtful, and well-supported curatorial assessments. * The final selection of exhibition projects will be made jointly by the MIFA Artistic Director and the Curators-in-Residence committee. **Exhibition Development** * Curate or support one or more exhibitions during 2027, depending on the exhibition schedule and the characteristics of each project. * Conduct studio visits and follow-up meetings with assigned artists. * Review portfolios, artist statements, artwork lists, and supporting research materials. * Define the final selection of artworks and the exhibition narrative in collaboration with the artist. * Develop the curatorial framework and proposed distribution of artworks within the gallery. * Write the curatorial essay, wall texts, labels, and any required interpretive materials. * Coordinate with the Artistic Director and the MIFA team on installation, lighting, signage, and the overall presentation of the exhibition. * Be present during the installation, opening reception, and principal public activities associated with assigned projects. * Participate in interviews, curatorial tours, public conversations, or promotional video content related to the exhibitions. * Ensure that each exhibition maintains MIFA's professional, curatorial, and presentation standards. **Institutional Participation** * Attend 68b2457229eb590d.description: Each year, the Résidence welcomes a dozen young directors to work on their first or second feature-length fiction film project, in two four-and-a-half month sessions. The Résidence offers its laureates the opportunity of devoting themselves to the writing of their feature films in a privileged setting in the heart of Paris. Over the four and a half months of their stay at the Résidence, every filmmaker is accompanied in the development of his or her script, and advised in the transition to production. The programme also includes a series of collective forums with industry professionals. Since it launched in 2000, the Résidence has welcomed over 300 filmmakers from more than 60 different countries, including Lucrecia Martel (Argentina), Lukas Dhont (Belgium), Corneliu Porumboiu (Romania), László Némes and Kornel Mundruczó (Hungary), and more. Many of the graduates from this 'Villa Médici' of the silver screen have gone on to be selected for international festivals: Nadav Lapid from Israel (Synonyms, Golden Bear 2019), Nadine Labaki from Lebanon (Capharnaüm, César and Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film 2019) and Michel Franco from Mexico (New Order, Grand Jury Prize at the Mostra 2020).
68b2457229eb590d.restrictions: other: The Festival's Résidence is open to young filmmakers who have made one or several short films, and no more than one feature film. Candidates must not be residents or citizens of France. There are two Résidence sessions every year, with each lasting four and a half months. The first session begins on 15 March and ends on 31 July. The second begins on 1 October and ends on 15 February. The filmmakers selected for the programme undertake to stay at the Résidence in Paris for the duration of the session.
68b2457229eb590d.title: The Résidence: devote yourself to writing

6cfc7cf59db361ef.description: PROJECT DESCRIPTION The Library and the ACC are requesting proposals for the commissioning of professional crosswalk mural designs throughout various locations in the City of Glendale with the intention of enhancing traffic safety in creative ways. In June 2023, the City of Glendale launched the pilot [Creative Crosswalks](https://www.glendaleartsandculture.org/creativecrosswalks) program as an example of utilizing art as a means for traffic calming, pedestrian safety and neighborhood improvement. The Creative Crosswalks program is in partnership with the Public Works Department (PW), with the goal of incorporating civic art into daily life. THEME: GLENDALE SISTER CITIES ​The theme for this Creative Crosswalks Request for Proposals is Glendale Sister Cities. The mission of the Glendale Sister Cities Program (managed by the Office of the City Manager) is to foster international understanding, promote cultural exchange, encourage educational collaboration, and build economic development partnership between Glendale and its designated sister cities. The City of Glendale currently has 11 sister cities and 4 friendship cities. The Arts & Culture Commission invites artists and artist teams to submit designs that celebrate the Glendale Sister Cities through proposals that honor the traditions, culture, landscape, cuisine and artistry of each city. All artistic genres are encouraged. Local and international artists and artist teams are encouraged to apply for this opportunity.
6cfc7cf59db361ef.restrictions: other: Local and international artists/artist teams of all artistic genres, arts organizations or schools may submit proposals.
6cfc7cf59db361ef.title: Creative Crosswalk Murals - Request for Proposals

6ddaacbd6bef4d4a.description: In the summer of 2027, the Hasselblad Foundation will, for the second time, inaugurate Sweden's largest photo salon - Fotosalongen 2027. We invite both amateur and professional photographers across all genres to submit their work through an open call, running from 1 August to 18 October 2026. The selection process will be conducted by a distinguished jury comprising Alexandra Ellis, curator at the Sune Jonsson Center for Documentary Photography, Västerbottens museum; Tarik Saleh, film director; Elisabeth Toll, photographer; and Dragana Vujanovic Östlind, Jury Chair and Chief Curator at the Hasselblad Foundation. Our objective is to curate an exhibition that showcases a diverse array of photographic styles and perspectives. The walls of the Hasselblad Center will be adorned with works that offer unexpected encounters and surprises, where the creations of established artists will be displayed alongside those of emerging talents and seasoned photographers who have yet to present their work publicly. This photo salon seeks to represent the full spectrum of contemporary photography, embracing practitioners whose interests span documentary and photojournalism, as well as nature, family, street style, science, politics, and the arts. Selection will not be confined to a specific theme; rather, it will focus on identifying compelling images and narratives that resonate with depth and diversity of expression. Our goal is to capture a comprehensive snapshot of current photographic practices.
6ddaacbd6bef4d4a.restrictions: other: You can apply for Fotosalongen 2027 if you turn 18 during the year of the application period, or are older, and are either Swedish citizen or have a residential address in Sweden. Both individuals and groups may participate.
6ddaacbd6bef4d4a.title: Hasselblad Foundation Fotosalongen 2027

6e53d4773985eb75.description: The Creative Catalyst Fellowship supports individual artists whose work engages the public on critical issues facing Asian American and Pacific Islanders (AAPIs) and can serve as a catalyst for civic participation. Selected artists join a cohort convened for peer sharing and learning, with access to communications consultation and promotion of their final work. **Up to eight artists will each receive $30,000 to produce work with the potential to break through to broader audiences and spark conversation around this year's theme: Belonging.** **Belonging** is a sense of community, home, agency, and the essential right for our communities to flourish. It is a counterweight to racism and violence, and it advances a vision of inclusion that recognizes the ways AAPI communities have shaped and contributed to this country. Art speaks to us, feels our pain, paints our dreams, and opens our minds in profound new ways. Our goal is to give independent artists the resources and freedom to do their art, in a way that also lets us put that art to work in the world. The Creative Catalyst Fellowship is a yearlong program, and Fellows are required to: * Attend a virtual orientation at the start of the program * Attend a two-day, in-person Creative Catalyst Fellows retreat on February 16 - 18, 2027 (location to be finalized; the AAPI Fund covers travel and accommodations) * Participate in virtual check-ins throughout the Fellowship * Submit a Narrative Report Fellows may also be invited to AAPI Fund events and asked to showcase their art, though attendance at these is optional. **Timeline** The fellowship program runs from January to December, 2027 _(all dates are subject to change)_ * **Informational Zoom webinar:** **Tuesday, September 1, 2026**, at 3:00 pm - 4:00 pm PT and **Friday, September 4, 2026**, at 12:00 pm - 1:00 pm PT. [Register for the webinar here.](https://us02web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_WuOLQFSWSI2XIp16hqjaOg#/registration) * **Creative Catalyst Fellows Retreat:** February 16 - 18, 2027 _(Required attendance)_ * **Artwork Completed:** August 15, 2027 * **Promotion of Completed Artwork:** August to December 2027

769495b565edd1a9.description: The Arts Center in Orange, VA, invites submissions for The Mini Masters Show, a juried group exhibition celebrating the power, intimacy, and innovation of small-scale works. The exhibition will feature 8" x 8" paintings by regional and national artists working across a wide range of media and styles. Exhibition Dates: December 4, 2026 - January 30, 2027 Artists are invited to submit three original 8" x 8" works. Any medium that can be framed and exhibited on a wall is welcome. All work must be submitted framed, except canvas works, which may remain unframed if edges are clean, finished, and professionally wrapped. All submissions must arrive ready to hang and are the responsibility of the artist for delivery and pickup. To create an accessible and collector-friendly exhibition, all accepted works will be offered for sale at a fixed price of $100 each. Sales will be split 50/50 between the artist and The Arts Center in Orange. Submission Guidelines * 5-10 images or time-based samples of recent work * Artist statement (300-500 words) * CV * Short biography * Optional reflection on the role of scale, intimacy, or time in your work * $20 submission fee - payable on our website * Submit materials through our website at: [www.artscenterinorange.com](http://www.artscenterinorange.com) under "Calls" or email [submissions@artscenterinorange.com](mailto:submissions@artscenterinorange.com) * Please include "Mini Masters" in the subject line * Deadline for submissions: October 1, 2026 Exhibition Vision _Mini Masters Show_ explores the unique visual and emotional impact of small works. In a cultural moment dominated by spectacle, scale, and speed, this exhibition asks viewers to slow down and engage more intimately with art. Small paintings possess a distinct kind of gravity: they invite close looking, reward attention to detail, and create a deeply personal encounter between artist and viewer. Historically, small-format works have served as studies, private meditations, devotional objects, keepsakes, and experiments in abstraction and observation. Yet these works are often among the most immediate and powerful forms of artistic expression. Scale does not diminish ambition. Instead, limitation can sharpen intention. This exhibition seeks artists who understand the poetic and conceptual possibilities of restraint - artists capable of creating works that feel expansive despite their dimensions. Whether minimal or densely layered, narrative or abstract, delicate or bold, the selected works will demonstrate how intimacy can carry equal weight to monumentality. By unifying all works within the same 8" x 8" format, _Mini Masters Show_ creates a visual conversation across mediums, styles, and perspectives. The exhibition emphasizes composition, precision, materiality, and presence, while encouraging viewers to move slowly through the gallery and discover the richness contained within each small frame. The fixed-price structure is intended to encourage new collectors, make original artwork broadly accessible, and create an energetic salon-style atmosphere where visitors feel invited to engage with and acquire contemporary art. By removing barriers around pricing and scale, the exhibition emphasizes connection, discovery, and the joy of living with original artwork. We welcome emerging and established artists alike whose work demonstrates originality, craftsmanship, and a compelling visual voice.
769495b565edd1a9.title: THE MINI MASTERS SHOW

7a29b6fa53e503e4.description: The Nordic Council of Ministers invites project proposals as part of Nordic Currents - a new international culture initiative to take place in 2027-2028. With trust, openness, artistic freedom and democratic values as its core, Nordic Currents invites cultural organisations in neighbouring European countries to join forces with Nordic partners and create projects that move audiences, deepen relationships and create lasting connections. Nordic Currents aims to showcase the richness and quality of contemporary Nordic culture and art in the neighbouring European countries as well as promote long-term collaborations between Nordic and European actors.

7a2db87e7826e2ef.description: In partnership with the New York State Canal Corporation (Canal Corp.), the Erie Canal Museum (Museum) is seeking two (2) Erie Canal Artists-in-Residence (AIR) for a period of one (1) year. While all artists are encouraged to apply, we are specifically seeking artists with ancestral ties to the Haudenosaunee Confederacy and/or Mohican Nation and artists who live or work in New York State Canal communities. The Residencies will focus on a year-long creative inquiry into the New York State Canal System - including the historic Erie Canal - reflecting on its past, contemplating its current condition, and considering its future. These Residencies are for Artists who wish to engage with the Canal and adjacent Canalway Trails, Canal Corp. and Museum staff, Canal facilities, New York's Canal communities, and Canal visitors. The 2027 Residencies will be dedicated to projects that reflect upon the Canal's physical, environmental, and social condition and history; materiality; and context. The Artist's project must directly address the Canal. Applicants shall propose a specific creative visual project for their Residency that must be able to be exhibited in a gallery setting. The subject of the project shall be identified by the applicant, but proposals must be a creative inquiry of the Canal and consider a fuller, more complete account of the Canal's past, present, and future than what has traditionally been told. The applicant shall identify their target audience(s) and how their project will be shared with that audience and with the public-atlarge. While studies of Canal communities are encouraged, the Canal and its context must be central to the project. Projects may focus on key areas of the Canal or the entire system. The New York State Canal System includes 524 miles of navigable waterways and 365 of multi-use trails. Artists should consider that scale when developing their proposal. **Residency Structure:** Two (2) Artists will be selected for Residencies in 2027. The NYS Canal Corp. will facilitate introductions and connections to Canal Corp. staff and access to Canal facilities as needed. The Residency will include an exhibition of the Artists' residency work at a museum/gallery venue TBD along the Canal corridor in 2028. Artists must engage with the public. The two (2) selected Artists will participate in two (2) joint virtual panels discussing their work. One panel will be a brief introduction in early 2027 during a program concluding the 2026 Erie Canal Artist Residencies, and the second panel will be in early 2028 in a program concluding the 2027 Erie Canal Artist Residencies and introducing the 2028 Artists. Artists will also participate in a reception for their exhibition in 2028. Artists must also develop, in collaboration with the AIR partners, at least one (1) additional public-facing event during the course of the Residency for the public to engage with and understand the Artist's process. The selected artists must coordinate a visit to the Museum and a tour with the Canal Corp. prior to submitting a work plan. While a project must be proposed as part of the application, a final work plan will be required by March 1, 2027. Each Artist's final project should include work that can be displayed in a gallery setting. Artists may incorporate text and other media into their work. It is intended that final projects from the Residencies will be used to develop a joint exhibition and catalog in 2028, as well as add to the Erie Canal Museum collection. Artists must deliver their work to the exhibit site by an agreed upon date, and the exhibit will be installed by museum/gallery staff. In consultation with the Artist, project organizers will retain work(s) from the project, as well as the right to publish, with prior Artist approval, selections from the project. Throughout the Residency, the Artist, Museum, and Canal Corp., will have regular virtual or in-person check-in meetings to assist in project development. It is expected that the Residency is a part-time commitment for the Artist. **Location:** The Artists shall focus on the New York State Canal system which includes the Erie, Oswego, Cayuga-Seneca and Champlain Canals, and the Erie Canalway Trail. A workspace is not included in this Residency
7a2db87e7826e2ef.place: 318 Erie Blvd E, Syracuse, NY 13202, USA

7d9535fb20ebf280.description: NARS Foundation is pleased to announce the continuation of our Curatorial Fellowship program, to run concurrently with the International Residency Program seasons. The Curatorial Fellow will work closely with the artists-in-residence and NARS Staff to develop an exhibition to be shown in the NARS Main Gallery each residency season. During the **two-season** fellowship period (Season I and II, January - June, 2027), curators will engage with the artists in residence to help them develop their work and the residency exhibition for two seasons of the International Artist Residency Program (two cohorts). Each International Residency season runs for approximately three months, and the exhibition developed by the curatorial fellow will be on view during the final month of each season. The Curatorial Fellow will conduct studio visits with each artist-in-residence and develop a cohesive curatorial plan for the group exhibition, with works from each of the current artists-in-residence. Curatorial Fellows are expected to be present in the studio space & NARS office for **at least two days a week**. This is a unique opportunity for emerging curators to work with artists from a multitude of backgrounds and disciplines. The Fellowship is designed to both complement and enhance the well-established International Residency Program, and further foster new perspectives and diversity of experiences for both the Curator and Residency Artists.
7d9535fb20ebf280.restrictions: other: Curators of any age, gender, and nationality are eligible to apply. Curators must be currently based in New York City, and have lived in NYC for at least 3 years. Emerging curators are highly encouraged to apply. Curators who are or will be enrolled in a college or university art degree-granting program during the Curatorial Fellowship period are not eligible to apply.
7d9535fb20ebf280.title: Curatorial Fellowship

7f3abf3011771b01.description: The **"9. Internationale Tanztheater Festival"** 2024 is behind us. Every two years, it is a great pleasure for us to present contemporary dance in the state capital of Erfurt. Our most recent festival was the most extensive since its inception in 2008. In addition to dance performances, cinema, a photo exhibition and workshops, we also hosted the **Federal Network Meeting Dance (Bundesnetzwerktreffen Tanz)**. The contemporary dance contest [contact.energy](http://contact.energy) '26 takes place at November 14, 2026. We invite all dancers and coreographers to apply with an unique and meaningful contribution to this year's edition of [contact.energy](http://contact.energy). After the success of the first contest during the 2. International Dance in 2010 we continue under the motto [contact.energy](http://contact.energy). The aim is to create a creative and exciting connection between the artist and the audience. The contest is part of the 10. International Dance Theatre Festival. A professional jury will evaluate the performances. The three most outstanding and compelling performances will receive an award. There will be also an audience award.
7f3abf3011771b01.title: contact.energy ́26

801f4f1a564fe72f.description: The Gibbes Museum and Society 1858's Prize for Contemporary Southern Art is awarded to an artist whose work contributes to a new understanding of art in the South. Presented annually, the Prize recognizes the highest level of artistic achievement and welcomes applications from artist working across any media. Artists who reside, work in, or are from Alabama, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maryland, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia and West Virginia are encouraged and eligible to apply (This includes the District of Columbia). Previous winners have subsequently received awards from the Joan Mitchell Fellowship, the Guggenheim Memorial Foundation, and the Pollock-Krasner Foundation Grant. Additionally, winning artists' work has been received into the permanent collections of The National Gallery of Art, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, and the Art Institute of Chicago, and the Gibbes Museum of Art.
801f4f1a564fe72f.restrictions: other: All artwork must be original to the artist in concept, design, and execution.
801f4f1a564fe72f.title: 1858 Prize for Contemporary Southern Art

80503cc1f74902eb.description: This residency open call is for an artist based in East Africa (Chagos Archipelago, Burundi, Comoros, Djibouti, Ethiopia, Eritrea, French Southern Territories, Kenya, Madagascar, Malawi, Mauritius, Mayotte, Mozambique, Réunion, Rwanda, Seychelles, Somalia, South Sudan, Uganda, United Republic of Tanzania, Zambia), who has already presented their work in several venues. The eleven-week, fully funded residency will take place at Gasworks in London from 7 April - 22 June 2027. Our residencies programme supports professional development, cultural exchange, and artistic experimentation. We host up to twenty residencies each year, bringing artists from all over the world to London. All our residencies are self-led, non-prescriptive and process-based; they are about enabling artists to research and develop new work, engage with the city, and build their networks. We provide administrative, pastoral, and curatorial support throughout the residency, but we expect residents to be self-motivated, and to lead on the research and production of their own work, during their time with us. We kindly ask applicants to carefully read the Application Guidelines and Residency FAQ (in the 'Resources' section below) before submitting their application. This residency is supported by **Mercedes Vilardell.**

80503cc1f74902eb.title: Residency open call for artists based in East Africa

81273a782865ee89.description: Dear Artist, Take your work beyond the studio and place it within the energy of Tokyo. **Art Seen is selecting 40 visual artists** for a collective digital billboard showcase at **Shibuya Crossroad**, one of Tokyo's busiest and most recognisable public locations. Selected artworks will appear together on a giant outdoor screen measuring approximately **3.34 metres high and 6.7 metres wide**. This is not a traditional gallery exhibition. It is an opportunity for your work to become part of the movement, lights and visual rhythm of Shibuya-seen in public rather than hidden online. Each selected artist will be included in the collective digital screen loop, with **22 rotations throughout the showcase day**. All artists will receive shared visibility as part of the same public presentation. The opportunity is open to visual artists working across painting, photography, illustration, digital art, graphic design, mixed media and other screen-ready visual practices. Artwork must be submitted in a **1:1 square format**, suitable for digital-screen presentation, as a high-resolution JPG or PNG file. All submissions must be appropriate for public display. Content involving nudity, violence, smoking, insulting material or other unsuitable imagery will not be accepted. **Key Details** **Location:** Shibuya Crossroad, Tokyo, Japan **Artist slots:** 40 **Showcase date:** 30 October 2026 **Application deadline:** 30 September 2026 **Format:** Collective public digital-billboard showcase **Screen dimensions:** Approximately 3.34 m × 6.7 m **Screen exposure:** 22 rotations throughout the showcase day **Artwork format:** 1:1 square, high-resolution JPG or PNG Your art deserves more than a scroll. Put it in the middle of Shibuya.
81273a782865ee89.title: Put Your Art on a Giant Screen in Shibuya

81d5c701dcea5a50.description: The Hambidge Center is situated on 600 forested acres in the mountains of north Georgia and offers miles of nature trails, meadows, waterfalls, a swimming hole and an abundance of wildflowers. The oldest residency program in the Southeast, Hambidge provides a self-directed program that honors the creative process and trusts individuals to know what they need to cultivate their talent, whether it's to work and produce, to think, to experiment or to rejuvenate. Residents' time is their own; there are no workshops, critiques, nor required activities. Each resident is given their own private studio which provides work and living space with a bathroom and full kitchen. The studios are designed to protect residents' time, space and solitude. Resident groups are intentionally kept small enough (8-10 people) to gather around the dinner table each evening, Tuesday through Friday, for delicious vegetarian meals prepared by our chef. These communal meals are an essential part of the Hambidge residency experience. Serious topics are discussed (and light-hearted ones, too), experiences are shared, and encouragement is given. Many a collaboration and life-long friendship have begun at the Hambidge dinner table. Members of each resident group come from different walks of life and work in different creative disciplines; from musicians, culinary artisans and scientists, to visual artists, writers, dancers and arts & culture administrators. Each year, residents of all ages come to Hambidge from over 30 states across the U.S., as well as internationally. Specialized equipment and facilities include the Antinori Pottery Studio, and a beautifully rebuilt turn-of-the-century Steinway grand piano housed in Garden Studio. **WHAT TO KNOW BEFORE YOU APPLY** * The studios are comfortable, but _rustic and secluded_. They are purposely simple, and most are out of sight of each other and somewhat isolated. * We are located in a forested environment. Residents should expect to occasionally encounter wildlife and insects - and sometimes the insects are inside the studios. * It is very dark at night. There are no street lights or ambient light, other than the moon and stars. * Due to our remote location, **there is no cell service at Hambidge**. Each studio has a phone for emergency, local and incoming calls. * To encourage focused creativity, **there is no internet in the studios.** WiFi is available 24 hours a day in the communal space of Lucinda's Rock House. **Length of Stay** Applicants may request stays between two weeks and eight weeks. Residents arrive on Tuesday and depart on Sunday. **Residencies of one week are available to Arts & Culture Administrator applicants and Culinary applicants ONLY.** Eight-week residencies will only be scheduled in the Fall and Spring Sessions. The maximum length of residencies awarded in Summer Session is four weeks. Because of differing lengths of individual stays, residents will arrive and depart on varying schedules. Hambidge accepts applications in the following disciplines: ARTS & CULTURE ADMINISTRATION - including proposals for professional projects and/or personal creative projects by administrators working for arts, culture or environmental organizations, or independently (a freelance curator, for example). It is not a requirement that the organization be a non-profit, however it must be an organization that works with or assists other people or produces public projects CULINARY ARTS - including recipe development, cookbook writing, food writing, food styling, food photography, and food preservation DANCE/CHOREOGRAPHY - including choreography, performance, and theory MUSIC/COMPOSITION - including composition, performance, vocal, and theory, in all genres of music PERFORMANCE - including performance art, theater, comedy, circus arts, puppetry/object theater, storytelling, spoken word/performance poetry, durational performance, ritual or community-based performance, and hybrid performance combining technology, video, sound, installation or visual art SCIENCE - this residency offers scientists in any branch of science a place to write and/or organize research CRAFT - includes ceramics, fiber and textiles, glass, jewelry, metalwork, wood, furniture, paper and book arts, leather, basketry, mixed-media craft, functional craft, craft-based installation, and printmaking. VISUAL ARTS - including book arts, conceptual art, design, drawing, environmental art, fiber arts, film & video, installation arts, metalworking, mixed media, multimedia art, painting, photography, printmaking, sculpture, and woodworking Note: We do not have darkroom, sculpture/woodworking, or printmaking facilities, but provide exploration space for artists working in those disciplines. Those working in wood or metal must bring their own tools and machinery. WRITING - including academic scholarship, criticism, fiction, history, poetry, journalism, nonfiction, philosophy, playwriting, screenwriting, storytelling **Multidisciplinary** If your proposal combines PROFESSIONAL expertise in more than one discipline, you will be asked to indicate the other discipline(s) that should be considered in the JUDGING of your proposal. Make sure your proficiency in each discipline is demonstrated in your submitted work samples. Expert jurors from all the indicated disciplines will be asked to judge your submission at an expert level. Examples: a journalist creating both written and photographic content; a graphic novelist; a ceramicist writing a guide to glazes. NOT, for example, a visual artist exploring scientific themes in their work.

We seek applications from emerging and mid-career creatives, as well as from those who are established with national and/or international reputations. Applications for residency are judged primarily on the quality of submitted work samples and professional promise. Hambidge accepts approx
