bf9cb4d22d7a1431.description: The Decatur Artway kicks off another year as Decatur's outdoor gallery, featuring dynamic sculptures scattered throughout the city of Decatur. Sculptures will be displayed on temporary loan for two years, creating an engaging rotating collection of public art around town. An interactive online map will permit public engagement and increase accessibility, and a plaque at each installation site will detail information about the artist and the sculpture The Decatur Artway is presented by the Decatur Arts Alliance in partnership with the Decatur Tourism Bureau and the Decatur Downtown Development Authority. Selected artists will be awarded an honorarium of $2,000. The installed work may be available for sale. Artwork sold as a result of the Decatur Artway will be subject to a 20% commission, which will be deducted from the purchase price and retained by the Decatur Arts Alliance. The sculpture must be available for the duration of the two-year contract. All submissions must be professionally constructed of durable materials which will withstand the elements. No maquettes or renderings will be considered for selection. We will only accept existing and ready-to-install works.
bf9cb4d22d7a1431.title: The Decatur Artway IX

bff70227f002cd40.description: Perform Europe is a funding scheme offering EUR 1.4 million for performing arts collaborations across all 41 Creative Europe countries. Perform Europe supports partnership proposals which reinvent the way we tour across borders. After two highly successful editions (2020-2022 / 2023-2026), Perform Europe will continue to put emphasis on exploring, with the performing arts sector, **how cross-border touring can be made fairer, greener, and more inclusive**. Keywords: performing arts, theatre, dance, performance, circus, outdoor arts, puppetry, interdisciplinary, change-makers, inclusion, diversity, fight against climate change, sustainability, fairness, cross-border mobility, innovation Do you have an innovative idea that resonates with these keywords? Read on!
bff70227f002cd40.restrictions: other: Proposals are submitted by collaboration partnerships of performing arts professionals and organisations. Partners should work on their proposal together. This is a call to the sector to create partnerships and propose **impactful** ideas that can generate real change via **two main priorities:** * **INCLUSION & DIVERSITY** * **FIGHT AGAINST CLIMATE CHANGE** Each proposal should choose **one of the above main priorities to focus on**, while still taking into account and implementing measures related to the **second priority.** In addition, all proposals should aim for **quality and inno
bff70227f002cd40.title: The Open Call

c03513dbef870aea.description: Dear Artist, This September, ARRIVAL Gallery will bring artists together in **Athens for a four-day exhibition** focused on presence, connection, and meaningful visibility. Set in one of Europe's most historic and creative cities, the Athens Showcase is designed for artists who want their work to be seen with care, not lost in an overcrowded space. **Location:** **Theodoritou Vresthenis, Efstratiou Pissa, Athens, 117 45, Greece** **Event dates:** **25th - 28th September 2026** **Deadline to apply:** **11th September 2026** A considered exhibition. A focused selection of artists. More space for the work to be noticed. If you've been looking for an international exhibition that feels human, calm, and artist-first, Athens could be the right place for your work. Submissions are now open. We'd love to see your work.
c03513dbef870aea.title: Show Your Art in Athens This September 2026

c10a4ccabbf0290d.description: The Visual Arts Fund is a grant program established in 2016 by Midway Contemporary Art with generous support from The Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts. Minneapolis-Saint Paul is one of thirty-nine cities and regions included in Warhol's Regional Regranting Program, which is aimed at promoting vibrant artistic activity in cities across the United States and Puerto Rico. In 2026 the Visual Arts Fund will award $60,000 (six $10,000 grants) to artist organized projects in the Twin Cities metro region. Proposals must name a lead organizer, but can include any number of artists as collaborators; individuals or groups may apply. The VAF supports the development of projects and initiatives that engage the public with visual art and seeks to support a wide array of innovative and diverse projects that otherwise might not occur. **What We Fund** * Projects that have a publicly accessible component * Projects could include exhibitions or installations held in temporary spaces, new publications, a series of events or performances, digital initiatives, public art projects, and other activities that are related to the visual arts **What We Do Not Fund** * An individual artist presenting exclusively their own work * Projects that are part of the programming of a 501(c)3 non-profit arts organization * Projects at a commercial gallery * Projects that do not offer an opportunity for free public engagement **Lead Organizer** If the project involves a group of artists working together, please choose one person to act as the Lead Organizer. The Lead Organizer will oversee the project and must play a key role in the creation and execution of the project. This contact person will also be responsible for receiving grant funds, communicating with Midway, and submitting the final survey. You may work with as many collaborators and/or artists as you wish. **2026 VAF Grant Timeline** Online Application Opens: Tuesday, September 1 Application Due: Saturday, September 26, 5pm (CDT) Grantee Notification: December 2026 Funding Awarded: January 2027
c10a4ccabbf0290d.restrictions: other: * Projects must function primarily within a visual arts context (rather than performing arts, music, literature, or other arts). While projects can have interdisciplinary elements, they must have a strong basis in the visual arts. * A publicly accessible component of the project must take place within the Twin Cities seven-county metro region. * Projects must be artist-organized and self-initiated; 501c3s, incorporated businesses, and students\* are not eligible to apply (\*PhD students are eligible). * Projects cannot charge admission or other fees to the public or to participants. * P
c10a4ccabbf0290d.title: Visual Arts Fund 2026

c39f762b0ebeca11.description: The Design Trust is pleased to announce the launch of the 2026-2027 Photo Urbanism Fellowship and the opening of a call for photographers. The theme of this cycle is connected to their latest project and publication, _Untaped_, focusing on the dynamic events and programs happening in New York City's public spaces.The Photo Urbanism fellow will create a new body of work on the theme of open and communal use of public space, present at a solo exhibition, and provide mentorship to a cohort of student photographers. The Photo Urbanism Fellow will dedicate 5% of their fellowship to administrative tasks such as attending meetings, invoicing, and tracking expenses; 10% of the fellowship to provide mentorship to young photographers; the remaining 85% will be to developing project work, including, but not limited to, photographing, editing images, developing programming, and exhibition planning. **End of Fellowship Deliverables:** * One comprehensive project proposal * One final solo exhibition, including a written description of work/project, minimum of 5 final images (digital and print; size to be determined) * Participation as a Visiting Critic during the Youth Photography Workshop Intensive for 6 CUNY Macaulay Honors College undergraduate students * At least one program related to project work, e.g., a talk or panel regarding the photography series.
c39f762b0ebeca11.restrictions: other: The Photo Urbanism Fellow must be based in New York City and be available to participate in meetings with the Design Trust, CUNY Macaulay Honors College, and the Youth Photography Workshop Intensive Teaching Fellow. The Design Trust will act as a resource and thought partner and will arrange two critiques and opportunities for feedback with local photographers. The fellowship requires a 9-month commitment, based on a mutually agreed-upon work plan. Applicants must be at least 21 years of age and eligible to work legally in the United States. Full-time students are not eligible due to po
c39f762b0ebeca11.title: Photo Urbanism Fellowship

c3a3faf32897fba2.description: The Lucid Art Residency Program encourages nonrepresentational artmaking exploration through mixed-media, conceptual, ecological, and interdisciplinary approaches. Nonrepresentational artwork does not represent or depict a being, place, or thing. The residency is a 3-week stay, usually between March and November, for artists in serene, retreat-like surroundings. This program encourages artists to delve into a contemplative state with their studio work. Solitary explorations in a remote place enable artists to unplug from their daily routines and find a deeper connection with nature. During the residency, artists have the opportunity to meet and dialogue with a Lucid Art professional artist associate who will visit the artist's studio and engage in conversation with them about their work. A weekly tea and conversation will be scheduled with staff, artist associates, and/or scholars. Artists will be given a tour of Gordon Onslow Ford's studio, shedding light on the historical and environmental context seeding the residency program and campus. Due to the limited number of artists who can attend per year, the Foundation would like to give opportunities to new artists. We only allow applications from artists who have not previously participated in our residency program.
c3a3faf32897fba2.restrictions: other: The Selection Committee will consider artists working in the visual arts, eco-art, video/new media, writing, poetry, music composition, and choreography. Applicants must: * Be 18 years or older and a resident of the US or Canada. * Have an MFA or equivalent in independent studio work and an exhibition history. * Have not been a Lucid Art Foundation artist-in-residence previously. * Have use of a car for transportation to, from, and during the entire solo residency. * Not use oil-based paints, turpentine, spray paint, or any media that are volatile or have strong odors during their resid
c3a3faf32897fba2.title: Lucid Art Residency Program 2027

c4b84f6107b6b3ae.description: The picturesque landscape has always captured the true beauty of nature, but can never look more beautiful than nature itself; however, whether it's the wild beauty of nature or the charm of small-scale details, this is your chance to show the world your perception of it. TERAVARNA's 14th International Landscape Juried Art Competition invites artists from all over the world. All forms or mediums of visual arts are acceptable, whether 2D or 3D. Winners will win up to $5,000 in cash prizes and international exposure on social media platforms. Indeed, the first, runner-up, and merit prize winners will also get the chance to get their artworks featured on ARTSY for free for six months. All the participants will be awarded a certificate of recognition as well. Artists can submit as many artworks as they like; the charge is $20 per entry. Submit your work before 30th September, 2026, and let your artwork reflect the spirit of the land. Please email us at [**info@teravarna.com**](mailto:info@teravarna.com) if you have any questions.
c4b84f6107b6b3ae.restrictions: other: The age at which participants may take part is 18 years. For those under 18 years of age, the participant will have to provide an NOC from their parent/guardian.
c4b84f6107b6b3ae.sculpture_why: tagged applied arts, public art, sculpture

c52298942698f246.description: **Grants for organizations, collectives and individuals to support free community-engaged arts programming at one of the Toronto Public Library branches.** **WHAT DOES THIS PROGRAM SUPPORT?** Created in 2014 as a partnership between Toronto Arts Council and Toronto Public Library, Artists in the Library program provides paid opportunities and space for Toronto artists while increasing access to the arts in Etobicoke, York, North York, East York and Scarborough through programming in the local library branches. Funding for this program is provided by the City of Toronto. Artists in the Library program provides funding to professional artists, arts organizations and collectives working in any artistic discipline to create and deliver free **community-engaged arts programming** at one of the branches of the Toronto Public Library. This program encourages applications from TAC's equity priority groups and **artists working in their local communities.** Grant recipients will have an opportunity to explore their art practice in a community setting; access space and facilities for arts programming and presentation; engage with the branch and its community in a meaningful way; work closely and be supported by the branch team; navigate a multi-stakeholder environment and create and deliver community-engaged arts programming from start to finish. Community engagement is a requirement in this program, but its format may vary. Activities may include exhibitions, installations, performances, concerts, screenings, readings, filmmaking, storytelling, workshops, artist talks, participatory programs, arts education and mentorship programs, and other arts programming. Permanent exhibitions and installations are not eligible. All funded projects will be produced by the grant recipient and hosted and supported by the assigned library branch. All projects must be delivered on site at the branch and within branch operating hours. **Project location:** There is no list of eligible branches in 2026. You can indicate interest in working at any branch outside of downtown core or simply select a geographic area or neighbourhood where you prefer to work, and the branch will be assigned to the funded projects by TPL staff, based on suitability and availability. [Areas](https://www.toronto.ca/city-government/data-research-maps/neighbourhoods-communities/community-council-area-profiles/) include: Etobicoke York, North York, Toronto & East York, Scarborough. For Toronto & East York, the downtown locations are not eligible: for the purpose of this grant program 'downtown' refers to the area south of St. Clair, east of Jane and west of Don Valley; if you have a question about specific location, please contact program manager. You can only propose programming for one branch. Note: if you included a specific preferred branch, a different branch might be assigned. **WHEN CAN THE PROJECT HAPPEN?** Programming in the branches must take place between September and December 2027.
c52298942698f246.restrictions: other: This grant program is open to **professional artists**, not-for-profit **arts organizations** or **artist collectives** operating on a not-for-profit basis. If you are a **first-time applicant** or have questions about your eligibility or your application, please contact the Programs Manager, Strategic Initiatives. Eligibility includes:[1](https://torontoartscouncil.org/grants/artists-in-the-library/#easy-footnote-bottom-1-196) **Eligibility criteria specific to Individuals:** If the applicant is an individual artist, the following eligibility criteria apply: * Individuals must be Canad
c52298942698f246.title: Artists in the Library

c5969cd71daad887.description: The LiftOff Residency takes place at NDA's Studio in Tribeca and **provides six physical-based performance artists with 30 hours of rehearsal space each**, an introductory meeting, and two feedback sessions. This residency is for artists looking to join a small cohort of artists to share and give feedback on each other's work. Fall/Winter LiftOff artists have access to book the studio from **November 5th, 2025 - January 30th, 2026**. Winter/Spring Liftoff artists have access to book the studio from **February 2nd, 2026 - April 30th, 2026**. Feedback sessions will be in-person. They are designed to share about creative process, project development, and participate in a community exchange. Feedback sessions are a space to present live work you are creating during the residency. Discussions regarding process, development, and production are also encouraged. LiftOff Artists will have an introductory meeting with NDA Executive and Artistic Director, Karen Bernard, at the beginning of the period to meet each other and schedule the two feedback sessions: one mid-residency and one at the end of the residency. The residency is only available for solo artists, or groups with up to 4 artists. The studio is located inside a personal residence, so studio hours are limited. **The studio is only available Monday - Friday: 10am-6pm. Please make sure this works with your schedule before applying. Weekends are not available to book.** Studio Regulations: * No live or loud music * No dancing with shoes unless approved * Props must be approved in advance * No more than four participants per artist/company Studio hours for Fall/Winter resident artists will start being reserved in October 2025 and hours for Winter/Spring resident artists will start being reserved in January 2026, in order to secure priority space booking.
c5969cd71daad887.restrictions: other: You must be a New York City based performance artist in order to apply.
c5969cd71daad887.title: LiftOff Residency

c677fcd3655f828b.description: Aegina Retreats offers a process-based artist residency on the island of Aegina, Greece, available from November to March. Residents are provided with dedicated studio workspace and may stay at the Grapevine House, located within walking distance of the studio, or in nearby independent accommodation. The residency supports painters, ceramic artists, sculptors, and material-based practitioners seeking uninterrupted time for research, development, and sustained engagement with their work. Residents work independently within a quiet studio environment, with the possibility of informal presentation in a local project space. The residency prioritizes continuity, focus, and immersion in the creative process.
c677fcd3655f828b.fee_note: 850 EUR - Studio residency with accommodation at the Grapevine House (shared occupancy), located within walking distance of the st
c677fcd3655f828b.title: Process-based studio residency on aegina island

c71c383b63122070.description: Akron Soul Train welcomes regional artists from various disciplines, encompassing visual, performing, and written arts, to submit their applications for residencies. Residencies are typically granted for a duration of one month, although they can be tailored to accommodate the artist's preferences and the scope of their proposed project, allowing for a shorter or longer duration for creation. Residency Responsibilities * Create a new body of work for public display * Create and lead a minimum of one community program during the residency * Availability for press and outreach opportunities * Post-residency survey completion Artists will be notified in November and a public celebration will take place at Akron Soul Train on Date TBD, from 5:00 - 7:30 pm.
c71c383b63122070.place: 191 South Main Street, Akron, OH 44308, USA
c71c383b63122070.restrictions: other: * Artists must be over 18 years of age * Artists must be regional (close enough to drive to Akron for events or be willing to travel for programming) Any artist who is able to travel to Akron to interface with our community for a public educational event (this can be virtual during the pandemic) and the final performance/exhibition will be considered for the residency. For example, artists that live in Pittsburgh, Detroit, and Columbus, or even farther, like Cincinnati, could consider themselves regional.
c71c383b63122070.title: 2027 Artist-in-Residence

c762d2fa570986a4.description: On 7 June 2026, the 12th International Awards for Art Criticism (IAAC 12) was officially launched at the Sichuan Fine Arts Institute, inviting submissions of art reviews in Chinese or English from around the globe. IAAC 12 is jointly run by the IAAC Organising Committee, the School of Philosophy at Fudan University, and the Shanghai Zhangyuan Art Museum (in preparation), with support from the Royal College of Art in London, the Edinburgh College of Art and the International Association of Art Critics (AICA). The IAAC 12 international jury comprises five members: * Fiona Bradley, Director, Fruitmarket, Edinburgh. * Ben Eastham, art critic and novelist based in London. He is the editor-in-chief of e-flux Criticism. * Richard J. Williams, Professor of Contemporary Visual Cultures at the University of Edinburgh. * WANG Pu, Associate Professor of Chinese Literature and Culture and Chair of the Department of German, Russian and Asian Languages and Literature, Brandeis University. * XIANG Zairong, Associate Professor of Comparative Literature and Director of Arts at Duke Kunshan University The Organising Committee of the International Awards for Art Criticism aims to support independent critical coverage of contemporary art, away from the immediate pressures of the market, media and private patronage. The Awards are to stimulate good writing, critical thinking and dialogue and research in China, the UK and wider afield. The objectivity of the selection process is underpinned, both by the recognised professionalism of the Chinese and English-speaking jury members and by the strict anonymity of the judging process.
c762d2fa570986a4.restrictions: other: **The Twelfth Edition is open to candidates from anywhere in the world writing in Chinese or English about any contemporary art exhibition held anywhere in the world or on-line between 1 September 2025 and 31 August 2026.** Candidates are invited to write a review of 1,500 English words or 2,500 Chinese characters on any exhibition of contemporary art. The submissions shall not previously have been published anywhere else.
c762d2fa570986a4.title: 12th International Awards for Art Criticism

c7d6fee1f0b39e25.description: The aim of Les antípodes is to foster critical thought and artistic experimentation through processes of research, creation, presentation and debate directed at exploring new ideas, associations and forms of expression, relation and experience. To this end, Les antípodes opens Numèric 2026: two research and creation residency grants in Agullana, Alt Empordà, addressed to artists, thinkers and scientists of all branches -formal, natural, social and applied- working in any field at the intersection of art, culture, science and thought. Numèric 2026 is a collaboration between Les antípodes and Bòlit, Centre d'Art Contemporani, Girona, and the Museu de l'Empordà, Figueres, with the support of the Generalitat de Catalunya, Agullana Town Council, Figueres Town Council and Acción Cultural Española (AC/E) through the PICE - Residencias nacionales programme.
c7d6fee1f0b39e25.restrictions: other: The call is open to everyone: it is addressed to artists, thinkers and scientists of any discipline and origin, both individually and as collectives. In the case of collectives, the stipend will be shared among the members. Applicants must be of legal age and able to reside in Agullana during the four weeks of the residency.
c7d6fee1f0b39e25.title: Numèric 2026

c882813da7ec7674.description: The residency within the creative hub Prostor is aimed at artists and cultural professionals working in the field of contemporary art. We especially encourage participatory, research- and process-based practices. **Topic for 2026: Unknown Objects, Spaces, Time** We accept applications on a rolling basis. Currently, we are accepting applications for short-term residencies through 2026!
c882813da7ec7674.title: Unknown Objects, Spaces, Time: 2026 Residency @ Prostor

caa336f06accf000.description: Zad is a support framework designed to promote mobility and communication for artists from the Arab region residing in Europe. Its main objective is to develop their artistic and professional path in collaboration with their peers and across various artistic spaces and platforms. Additionally, Zad assists artists in reaching and engaging with different types of audiences, all while enhancing their contributions to public life within the cities and countries in which they reside and work. Zad's support covers all artistic and literary specialisations and is open to individuals of all ages. d21cc780a4132e20.description: **This year's PhotoVogue Global Open Call embraces creativity as rebellion, inviting photographers and video makers to use image-making to challenge indifference, disrupt conventions, and expand visual storytelling.** This open call does not ask for a theme to illustrate. **It asks for a position**. It asks for a position in relation to the world as it is. In relation to what one refuses. In relation to what one longs for, questions, resists, imagines, or defends. There is no single answer. It may take the form of intimacy, care, or attention. It may take the form of confrontation, rupture, or refusal. It may involve invention, disobedience, new visual languages, new aesthetics, and the imagining of new worlds. What matters is not whether the work belongs to fashion, art, documentary, photography, or video. What matters is the force, the urgency, and the necessity behind it. To create in this context also means allowing oneself a deeper freedom. A freedom from repetition. A freedom from expectation. A freedom from approval. It means creating without the need to please. At a time when so much is made to disappear into the stream, this open call is an invitation to resist that disappearance. Create from urgency, not habit. Create from conviction, not compliance. Do not illustrate the world as it is. **Answer it.**
d21cc780a4132e20.restrictions: other: We welcome photography, video, and multimedia projects across all genres and from around the world, including fashion, documentary, portraiture, fine art, and experimental practices. We are looking for work that expresses a clear point of view, whether through the ideas it explores, the emotions it evokes, or the strength of its visual language. This can take many forms, from powerful storytelling to images that stand out for their aesthetic impact. ❌ **AI-generated works are not eligible.**
d21cc780a4132e20.title: Brave New Visions: Creativity as Rebellion

d5c37e0861b43dff.description: The Art in Public Places Program of New Mexico Arts at the NM Department of Cultural Affairs (NMDCA), in collaboration with Spaceport America seek an artist/artist team to create a public art sundial - a functional work of art. The sundial artwork will be installed outside the newly built STARC (Spaceport Technology and Reception Center) at Spaceport America, an earthbound but aspirational space dedicated to inquiry in the high desert southwest of New Mexico. The intent of the sundial is to creatively represent the origins of measurement and human curiosity. At its essence, a sundial is a chronometric device that translates Earth's rotation into a visual, accurate representation of time. By intercepting the sun's rays, it uses the position and length of a shadow to indicate the hour, essentially serving as a bridge between celestial mechanics and terrestrial life. Sundials are at least 3,500 years old. In this installation, the sundial acts as a functional work of art, reminding us that time is not merely a digital abstraction but a physical consequence of humanity's journey through the solar system. It connects the cosmos, the blue sky, the sun, and the vast, beautiful Jornada de Muerto basin to the mechanical and tactile realism of Spaceport America. It should evoke curiosity and wonder. A sundial is the ancestor of the clock, the calendar, and the computer. It is one of humankind's first attempts to understand the universe. People in New Mexico, no matter who they are or when they live, have always honored the workings of the cosmos. * Interactivity: More than just a work of art, a sundial invites the observer to engage with the environment and with time itself. It highlights the changing seasons through the shifting length of the shadow - long and sweeping in winter, short and sharp in summer. It should spark curiosity about cosmic motions. * Symbolism: It stands as a monument to constancy. While technology evolves, the relationship between the sun and the Earth remains the most reliable metronome in human history. A sundial attests to both the motion of the Earth in relation to the sun and the consistency of that motion over the centuries. * Artistry: The artist/artist team has the choice of evoking other feelings and emotions about time, space, technology, the vast desert and sky, and the human condition, as we reach for the stars at New Mexico's Spaceport. A sundial consists of two fundamental components that work in tandem: 1. The Gnomon: Derived from the Greek word for "one who knows," the gnomon is the vertical or angled element that casts the shadow. In a scientifically accurate installation, the gnomon's angle is typically set to the latitude of its location, aligning it parallel to the Earth's axis of rotation. 2. The Dial Plate: The surface onto which the shadow is cast. This plate is inscribed with hour lines and, often, seasonal markets. As the sun moves across the sky from east to west, the shadow moves across the plate in the opposite direction. During the peak of the sun's arc, the sundial will indicate the solar noon. Artists may interpret these elements as they see fit to fulfill their artistic vision, while maintaining the elements that would keep this artwork a functioning sundial. The intent of this open competition is to select finalists that demonstrate highly unique and creative expressions of historical and/or scientific objects and their functions, while evoking a sense of wonder by the viewer. The high desert open landscape invites experimental but functional approaches to this important object of measurement.
d5c37e0861b43dff.restrictions: other: This REQUEST FOR QUALIFICATIONS is open to all artists/artist teams currently residing in the United States. Artists submitting qualifications should demonstrate a level of experience and professionalism that is commensurate with the project scope and budget.
d5c37e0861b43dff.title: Spaceport America Sundial Public Art Project

d64594322d6f5cbd.description: As an international research institution, the CCA operates in the spaces between architectural culture at large and academic discourse through exhibitions, publications, public events, and research programs. The CCA's Research Fellowship Program supports innovative, advanced research to foster new kinds of intellectual exchange that spark long-term dialogue and debate. At the CCA, we are addressing a range of topics relevant to architectural discourse. Current topics of particular interest include: the infrastructural dimensions of built and natural environments; land management practices across geographical contexts and time periods; the relationships between architecture and new media, particularly through generative AI; and African diasporic networks across pedagogy and practice. **The program** Research Fellows are offered a residency at the CCA between June and August for a period of one to two months, with the goal of creating a community of researchers on site, particularly alongside our [Doctoral Research Residency Program.](https://www.cca.qc.ca/en/41082/doctoral-research-residency-program) Based on the scope of the proposed research project, the CCA's curatorial committee will determine the duration of the residency in discussion with each candidate to best support their project. In addition to a public presentation of their work in progress, Research Fellows are expected to participate in discussions, seminars, and workshops organized at the CCA, exchange with CCA staff, and engage with the local academic and architectural community. Research Fellows should be in residence for one to two months. The residency window is between 7 June to 30 July 2027, with prospective fellows required to accommodate a start date during the second or third week of June. Research Fellows are expected to be in residence at the CCA during their tenure and to be active participants in the summer events at the CCA. This harmonized fellowship period allows the fellows more in depth access to the CCA Collection and for exchanges across their research projects.

d761b93e4fa8e83e.description: **BIBLIOTECA INVISIBILE** **International Open Call for Artists** **MEDIT.A - Mediterraneo Arte | Siracusa, Italy** **Deadline: 15 November 2026** **THE OPEN CALL** MEDIT.A - Mediterraneo Arte launches **Biblioteca Invisibile**, an international contemporary art project that explores the Mediterranean as a shared space of memory, identity, migration, cultural heritage and exchange. The project brings together artists from **Italy, Africa and the wider Mediterranean**, creating a collective artistic narrative in which different cultures, generations and artistic languages can meet. The exhibition will take place in **Siracusa, Sicily**, from **June to December 2027**, at the **Palazzo del** **Governo di Siracusa**. **THE THEME** Artists are invited to interpret the Mediterranean as a space of relationships, memories and cultural exchanges. The central concept is the **artist's book**, understood not as a traditional publication, but as an **autonomous artwork and narrative device**. We are looking for works that explore, through contemporary artistic languages: • memory and identity; • belonging and migration; • intangible cultural heritage; • languages and traditions; • cultural exchange and contamination; • dialogue between different territories and communities. **WHO CAN APPLY** The Open Call is open to: • emerging contemporary artists; • independent artists; • independent artistic collectives. Particular attention will be given to artists from **Africa, Italy and the wider Mediterranean** **region**.**ARTISTIC LANGUAGES** The following media are accepted: • painting; • sculpture; • photography; • video art; • installation; • new media; • mixed media; • experimental practices. **One artwork per artist.** Maximum dimensions for physical artworks: **30 × 30 × 30 cm**. Video works: duration between **3 and 5 minutes**. **SELECTION** The artworks will be evaluated by an **international jury composed of 7 professionals**, including curators, art historians, critics and cultural professionals. The selection will consider: • artistic quality and originality; • strength of the artistic research; • conceptual coherence; • ability to address themes of memory, identity and intercultural dialogue; • relationship between the artwork and the Mediterranean and African cultural context. Approximately **22-40 artists** will be selected. **PREMIO BIBLIOTECA INVISIBILE** One selected artist will receive the **Premio Biblioteca Invisibile**. **The prize includes:** **A solo exhibition at Leucò Art Gallery ETS in Siracusa, Italy, lasting approximately 30 days.** The Award aims to enhance and internationalise the artist's career and to foster new relationships within the MEDIT.A cultural network. **APPLICATION** The application must include: • CV;• portfolio; • artist statement; • technical sheet of the submitted artwork; • images and/or video; • completed application form. **Application fee: €35** Shipping costs, customs duties, return and insurance of the artwork are the responsibility of the selected artist. Applications must be submitted by email to: [**opencalleuco@gmail.com**](mailto:opencalleuco@gmail.com) **KEY DATES** **Open Call:** 1 September - 15 November 2026 **Selection:** January 2027 **Announcement of selected artists:** 20 February 2027 **Artwork shipment:** 15 March 2027 **Exhibition opening:** 19 June 2027 **Project conclusion:** 30 December 2027 **MEDIT.A - MEDITERRANEO ARTE** **Biblioteca Invisibile** is the inaugural project of MEDIT.A - Mediterraneo Arte, an international programme dedicated to contemporary art, intercultural dialogue and cultural cooperation between Italy, Africa and the wider Mediterranean. The project forms part of a long-term process aimed at the creation of a future **Museum of the** **Mediterranean**. The artwork may be donated by the artist and, in that case, will become part of the permanent collection of the new **MEDIT.A Museum**.
d761b93e4fa8e83e.title: Biblioteca Invisibile

e1f2cf304b5582d4.description: Wonder Mountain Open Source Space Residency welcomes LGBTQIA+ and BIPOC artists and creators to an immersive two-week program offered year-round. This residency embraces a wide spectrum of visionaries-writers, visual artists, musicians, filmmakers, performers, designers, digital innovators, cultural workers, community builders, healers, curators, scientists, and multidisciplinary makers of all kinds. We also encourage groups and collectives to apply, as well as those who wish to facilitate community-engagement workshops. Set in the wide-open desert landscape of Wonder Valley, California-just a short drive from Joshua Tree National Park-our space offers both stillness and inspiration. Here, creators can step away from the noise, reflect and reset, nurture bold new ideas, and reconnect with the elemental cycles of nature and cosmos. We encourage artists and writers seeking a quiet and inspiring rural desert environment to apply to Wonder Mountain Open Source Space. Our space is surrounded by the plants and creatures of the Mojave: Yucca brevifolia is indigenous to the region and isn't found anywhere else in the world. Come see the desert flowers in bloom as the meteor showers explode in the darkness and stillness of Wonder Valley. Wonder Mountain Open Source Space encourages creative professionals of all backgrounds to apply for admission. The space is centered on principles of self-reflexive artistic practice that embraces the healing elements of the land as a site of reciprocal action. We envision an aesthetics of generosity, compassion, and an astral breadth of scope that seeks to nourish the creative spirit in all producers who venture to travel here. The space is located on the traditional ancestral homelands of the Serrano, Cahuilla, Chemehuevi and Mohave (Mojave) indigenous communities, the land that encompasses what's known as so-called Joshua Tree National Park, Twentynine Palms, and Wonder Valley. We at Wonder Mountain Open Source Space acknowledge the Serrano, Cahuilla, Chemehuevi and Mohave (Mojave) indigenous people, the traditional custodians of this land. We recognize the ongoing impact of colonization and displacement on Indigenous communities. We honor their deep connection to this place and their enduring stewardship of the land and waters.
e1f2cf304b5582d4.restrictions: other: At this time we admit international and US-based artists over the age of 21 working in the following mediums: Writers (poetry, fiction, screenplays, creative nonfiction, more), Photographers, Filmmakers, Healers and Wellness Practitioners, Movement/Choreographers, Astrologers, Curators, Earth Scientists, Activists, Musicians and Composers. We are currently working to provide more resources in the future for Visual Artists, Painters, and Ceramic artists.
e1f2cf304b5582d4.title: Two-Week Rural Desert Residency

They shape how work is read, shared, and, ultimately, remembered. In a moment defined by accelerated image flows and shifting economies of attention, the photobook remains a place for slowness, intention, and depth, where visual language can unfold on its own terms.

We are interested in publications that engage critically with contemporary life, visual culture, and the politics of representation, as well as those that foreground materiality, design, and storytelling as integral to the work. This call is open-ended by design. Rather than prescribing a theme, we invite you to contribute to an ongoing conversation about contemporary photobook culture. **Please not
e362839be5be804d.title: In Focus: Photobook Feature

e37fd906db70ca8b.description: As part of the new Digital Hubs initiative of the Conseil des arts et des lettres du Québec (CALQ), the [Society for Arts and Technology (SAT)](https://sat.qc.ca/en/) is launching a new research-creation residency program. This program aims to offer artists a space for technological exploration and innovation, free from the constraints and pressure to deliver results that are typically associated with production residencies. We will support three projects that will bring live arts and technological arts into dialogue around human movement. This program is open to non-profit organizations, collectives, and individual artists. It offers personalized support from the SAT teams over a two-month period, access to the facilities of the Society for Arts and Technology (SAT), as well as a $10,000 grant. This program is intended for artists and collectives who wish to explore, experiment with, and develop an immersive artistic practice combining arts and technology, using cutting-edge or experimental technologies, without necessarily aiming to produce a finished work in the short term. We will help you select and learn how to use the technological tools relevant to your project, and understand their limitations and possibilities, in order to carry out a research-creation phase.
e37fd906db70ca8b.place: 1201 Boulevard Saint-Laurent, Montréal, QC H2X 2S6, Canada
e37fd906db70ca8b.restrictions: other: The residency is open to professional artists and artistic collectives from around the world, regardless of their level of experience or primary discipline, provided they have a profile and a project suited to immersive technologies. The team must also submit a joint portfolio demonstrating its autonomy and ability to carry out the creative project, particularly with regard to visual and sound creation within a dome.
e37fd906db70ca8b.title: Research-creation residency program in arts & technologies

e737fc26ad1c8789.description: **Artists are invited to submit work for exhibition alongside members of the Royal Institute of Oil Painters at the ROI Annual Exhibition 2026** The Royal Institute of Oil Painters was founded in 1882 and is the only major British art society that promotes and exhibits work of the highest standard exclusively in oil paint. The ROI Annual Exhibition features work by many exciting emerging painters alongside the work of more established names. **Works on a Theme: Winter Rituals** This year's special theme is 'Winter Rituals', for which The ROI Themed Painting Prize is on offer to the best interpretation. The theme invites oil painters to explore the traditions, repeated actions, gestures and rhythms that shape our experience of winter, from personal routines and acts of devotion to cultural traditions and collective gatherings. It reflects on the character, moments, identity and symbolism of contemporary life. N.B. The theme is optional, one aspect of a larger exhibition, to which oil paintings of all subjects are welcome.

eb4d9198a0cbddd1.description: The Michigan Society of Fellows (MSF) invites applications to a new Arts Initiative fellowship it is piloting. Along with its customary six annual fellowships in the sciences, social sciences, and humanities, MSF will support one dedicated fellowship position in the arts for both the 2027-2030 and 2028-2031 fellowship terms. Founded in 1970 as a place for scholars and artists newly emerging from graduate school to pursue research and creative projects while participating in wide interdisciplinary conversation, the Society has long included artists among its fellows, and now seeks to be even more deliberately inclusive of artistic practice. For the first time, to increase arts applications, we will dedicate a seventh position expressly for a creative fellow. This three-year, residential fellowship is open to candidates who have completed an MFA degree or comparable terminal degree in the arts since June 2024 and who wish to pursue creative work and research opportunities while teaching at a major research university. In its first pilot year, the Arts Initiative fellowship will be available in the following participating departments: 1) Creative Writing / English Department and 2) Film, Television, & Media. Applicants whose creative practice align with these fields are encouraged to apply. Fellows are appointed as non-tenure-track Assistant Professors in appropriate departments and as Postdoctoral Scholars in the Michigan Society of Fellows for a three-year term to begin August 25, 2027. They teach the equivalent of one academic year of courses spread across the three-year fellowship term. The annual salary will be $63,000 plus an annual $3,000 research stipend. The Society of Fellows and the University of Michigan recognize and value contributions to the processes of identifying and addressing the social, environmental, and technical challenges our societies and our planet face. We encourage applicants to comment in their creative proposal on how their research, teaching, service, creative practice, and outreach activities contribute to analyzing and tackling such challenges.

eb4d9198a0cbddd1.title: Arts Initiative Fellowship with U-M Society of Fellows

ec25f1b55d482775.description: "Raccont'arti" is a free international open call for photographers and visual artists, aimed at mapping the state of contemporary photography. The 2026 edition explores **"Beyond the visible: the image of absence"**. The Prize invites artists to investigate absence not as subtraction, but as a stratification of space and time. Works should map what remains when action subsides, treating space as an active infrastructure of signs and interactions. The call includes two categories: **Open**, for all artists, and **Student**, for those currently enrolled in art schools or who graduated within the past year.
ec25f1b55d482775.title: Contemporary Photography Award

efaa2386890c8cbf.description: For our upcoming issue, we are looking for **drawings** that approach the city in all its forms: as a place, a system, a social structure, an organism, a memory or an idea. It might appear through maps, public space, housing, transport, migration, displacement, urban nature, borders, crowds, solitude or everyday life. It may be real, remembered, imagined, invented or yet to come. Cities are never fixed. They are constantly built, transformed, expanded, neglected and remade. Shaped by architecture and infrastructure as much as by movement, politics, ecology and the people who inhabit them, they carry traces of the past while continually making room for possible futures. Cities bring different lives into proximity. People meet, pass one another, share spaces, remain strangers or build communities. Neighbourhoods evolve, buildings disappear and new structures emerge. The visible city is only one layer of a larger network of relationships, histories and invisible systems.
efaa2386890c8cbf.restrictions: other: We welcome a broad range of approaches and interpretations. Drawing can observe, document, analyse, question, speculate or reinvent the urban world. It can focus on the visible fabric of the city or reveal the forces, tensions and hidden structures that shape it.
efaa2386890c8cbf.title: OPEN CALL FUKT #24 - THE CITY ISSUE

f0f55d529f1ab1f0.description: Leica Society International (LSI) is proud to announce its tenth annual _Photography Grant_. The LSI Grant was established in 2017 to provide financial support for deserving photographers who are in the process of creating or completing a personal photographic project. This grant is open to all photographers (where allowed by law) and is made possible through LSI and Leica Camera North America. **Grant Theme: "To Be Seen"** _To Be Seen_ invites photographers to submit in-progress, personal projects that explore what it means to see and be seen. We are looking for work in still-images that create space for people, places, communities, histories, or issues to be witnessed with care, dignity, and intention. **Strong submissions should show:** * Who or what is being seen * What has kept this story unseen, unseen clearly, or misrepresented * What changes when the subject is witnessed with care * How the photographer creates trust, presence, and respect through the work * What the images reveal about dignity, identity, agency, or belonging * At its core, this theme asks: What becomes possible when a person, story, or community is truly seen.
f0f55d529f1ab1f0.restrictions: other: The LSI Photography Grant is open to photographers who are at least 18 years old on or before July 24, 2026. Use of a Leica camera is not required; membership in LSI is not required. **This is a global program.**
f0f55d529f1ab1f0.title: LSI 2026 Photography Grant - To Be Seen

f386679de6724147.description: _How does our perception change when we know nothing about the artist behind a work? How do we determine the value of a drawing when every work is offered at the same price? Where is the boundary between art and non-art?_ "Anonymous Drawings" is an exhibition project that puts these questions into practice. The exhibition at "ZAK - Zentrum für Aktuelle Kunst" in Berlin, Germany will feature around **600 drawings by 600 international artists, without revealing their names or the titles of the works.** Participation is free and open to everyone. Each exhibition is preceded by an international open call. There are no thematic requirements; the only limitation is a maximum format of A3 (29.7 x 42 cm). Biographical information is not requested. Selection is based solely on anonymized digital images. Only selected artists are asked to send their original drawings to Berlin. "Anonymous Drawings" is both a conceptual artwork and an exhibition platform: a collective artwork without hierarchies that continually rethinks the relationship between art, the market, and the public.
f386679de6724147.restrictions: other: **Anonymity is maintained until a work is sold.** Once sold, the drawing is removed from the wall, and the empty space is filled with the artist's name and place of origin.
f386679de6724147.title: Anonymous Drawings 2027

f78e1bedb8c9d193.description: This annual prize is open to all professional photographers on the French scene (French creators or artists working and/or residing in France, regardless of their nationality) developing an auteur photography. A grant of 6,000 euros will support the winning photographer in finalizing an ongoing photographic series that combines photography (in all its forms) and science (all disciplines), in France and/or abroad. The winning project will be presented in the form of an exhibition at Villa Pérochon CACP in the fall of 2027. The winner will receive display rights for this exhibition worth 1,000 euros and the production will be directly managed by Villa Pérochon CACP up to 2,000 euros (production within the Villa Pérochon laboratories or via an external provider). Following the first exhibition, Villa Pérochon will do everything possible, in conjunction with the winner, to facilitate the circulation of the existing exhibition within cultural structures, including those of the Diagonal network, a national network bringing together structures for the production and dissemination of contemporary photography in France (the cost of transporting the works round trip and the remuneration of the winner will be covered by the host structure). The winner will also benefit from dedicated communication with media partners. The presentation of the complete series will also be the subject of a round table discussion with screening at ADAGP in Paris (attendance of the winner is mandatory).

The jury will select only one ongoing, unfinished photographic series that fully integrates photography and science. We champion innovative and diverse artistic expression, offering a personalized, appointment-only experience. This approach allows visitors to deeply engage with thought-provoking works. Situated in [Bushwick](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/dcla/downloads/pdf/BCC-NACI-Bushwick.pdf), the art capital of New York City and a neighborhood adjacent to Williamsburg, Brooklyn, Bushwick Gallery is at the epicenter of NYC's dynamic art scene. Bushwick boasts a fresh, cutting-edge artistic vibe with numerous studios but very few galleries. Artists live, dream, and work in our vibrant location, making it a hub for creativity. Bushwick Gallery [features](https://bushwickgallery.com/featured-artists/) a wide array of exhibitions showcasing both renowned and emerging artists from around the globe. Our program includes various media such as paintings, sculptures, and installations. Each exhibition inspires and challenges perceptions. **Supporting Artistic Growth and Innovation** At Bushwick Gallery, we dedicate ourselves to supporting artistic growth and innovation. Our mission is to create opportunities for artists to expand their practice and reach new audiences. By highlighting the diversity of art, our exhibitions reflect the unique spirit and energy of New York City and the creative communities of Bushwick and Williamsburg. Explore the cutting edge of art at Bushwick Gallery, your go-to destination for art in NYC. fa2b43ce0b81d76a.description: Show us your most powerful photographic project. Rotterdam Photo invites photographers worldwide to submit bold, original work for our 2027 festival within the theme Vibrance. Be part of an international celebration of photography in the heart of Rotterdam. Theme 2027: VIBRANCE - The Pulse of a Living World Vibrance is an exploration of energy in its many forms - from the intimate to the collective, from physical presence to digital intensity. In a time where narratives are often shaped by crisis and fragmentation, this theme turns toward what continues to move, connect, and generate meaning. Vibrance is not only movement, but tension, rhythm, resistance, and transformation. It exists in bodies coming together, in cities in flux, in cultural expression, and in the invisible forces that shape everyday life. We invite photographers to interpret Vibrance freely - as a social condition, emotional state, visual rhythm, or conceptual framework. Your vision. Our city. Your moment. Enter Rotterdam Photo 2027.

fd5e466f2bbf9c74.description: With the support of UNSEEN, Picter, and Form Magazine, we are proud to launch the Form Photo Award x UNSEEN 2027, dedicated to contemporary photography. This annual award seeks to support emerging voices, distinctive visual approaches, and critically engaged photographic practices. The initiative aims to encourage international exchange and sustained dialogue within the contemporary photography community. In previous years, alongside receiving a cash prize, winners of the Form Photo Award exhibited their projects in Paris, at Miami Scope during Art Basel Miami Beach, and at photo basel during Art Basel Basel. In 2027, selected winners will receive free participation in UNSEEN 2027 during Art Rotterdam. Exhibiting at one of Europe's leading contemporary art fairs-attended annually by thousands of gallerists, curators, collectors, critics, and photography professionals-offers an opportunity to present work in an international context and engage directly with key figures in the field of contemporary photography.
fd5e466f2bbf9c74.restrictions: other: **The Form Photo Award is open to photographers:** * professionals or amateurs, art school students or the school of photography, independent photographers. * all nationalities. * over 18 years old.
fd5e466f2bbf9c74.title: Form Photo Award x UNSEEN

ff6bab9aab1cd570.description: Applicants are asked to submit their work to ONE of the following five award categories: **Still Image >** A single image work, or interconnected series of images, created through digital processes such as generative imagery, scanning technology, photo manipulation, illustration graphics, or renders of 3D models or virtual worlds. **Moving Image >** A moving image work created through digital processes, including but not limited to video, animation, machinima, and GIF art. **Screen-Based Interactive >** An interactive work experienced on a screen such as a computer, tablet, or mobile phone, including but not limited to game art, web art, and generative simulations. **Extended Reality (XR) >** A virtual, augmented, or mixed reality work experienced through a smartphone, tablet, or headset, or as a 360-degree video. **Digital Installation >** A multi-component, primarily screen-based work produced and presented with digital technologies that engages audiences in physical space and combines moving image, sound, interactivity, and/or movement.
